News.title: Record 230 people cross Channel in one small boat
News.content:
Tap the questions below

How many people cross the English Channel in small boats?

Between 1 January and 8 August 2026, a total of 14,819 people crossed the English Channel by small boat from France. This was down by 43% on the same period the previous year.

These crossings have become the most common way for people to be detected entering the UK illegally since 2020.

Nearly all those who arrive by small boat claim asylum. Under international law, this means they are allowed to stay in the country while their asylum application is considered.

Small boat arrivals made up 42% of asylum applications between April 2025 to March 2026.

Boats that arrived in the UK from 9 August 2025 to 8 August 2026 carried an average of 67 people. This has more than doubled since 2021.

Experts say overcrowding in boats makes crossings riskier. At least 84 people died while attempting to cross the Channel in 2024, according to the United Nations (UN).

When looking at the scale of small boats crossings, the number of these arrivals is about 5% of the size of total immigration into the UK from January 2025 to December 2025.

The government has pledged to âsmash the gangsâ behind these crossings in order to reduce the numbers.

News.title: Travelodge staff gave domestic abuser key to his victim's room
News.content:
Another woman, Jo from Leeds, contacted BBC News following coverage of the Maidenhead attack.

In July, she woke in her room to an unknown man standing at the end of her bed, and screamed for help.

"It was just horrible, it was horrendous. Terrifying. I was shaking so badly," she said.

Her friend who was staying in the room heard him say, "I'm sorry, they gave me this key," she said.

Jo considered staying elsewhere following the reports of the attack in 2022, but was reassured by Travelodge's chief executive Jo Boydell, who previously said: "The safety and security of customers in our hotels is extremely important and we want everyone to be safe, and feel safe, in our hotels."

Jo said: "What happened to us shouldn't have happened. And the assurances [Travelodge] gave are not accurate. The systems are failing."

In response, Travelodge said an investigation found "our updated room access security policies, which were in place at the time, were not correctly followed, which is not acceptable.

"We have retrained the hotel team on our current room security and check-in procedures."

Andy Smith, who has travelled the country with his band and stays in dozens of Travelodge hotels a year, said he had been given keys to other people's rooms recently.

"We went up to the room and there was a guy already asleep in there in a state of undress," he said.

It followed another incident about 18 months ago where another man had gained access to his room by telling reception staff he was checking in under a common name such as "Mr Smith", Andy Smith said.

"I think he just chanced it. Because my name's Smith, I think it's just the pure luck of it. I mean, why wouldn't anyone be asking for ID or anything, like a booking reference or an email address. It beggars belief."

Travelodge responded by saying "any case of an unauthorised person entering a guest's room is a significant cause for concern and we want to be clear that these incidents should not have happened".

News.title: Thames Water gave finance boss a £1m signing-on fee
News.content:
Thames Water paid its finance chief a Â£1m signing-on fee in July as the company struggles with a mountain of debt and faces temporary nationalisation.

Steve Buck joined the company in April 2025 but it is understood the seven-figure payment was not made until last month after the company had taken legal advice over its contractual obligations.

The existence of the payment, first reported by Sky News,, external was apparently revealed in a letter from the Thames Water chairman to MPs on the Commons Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee.

The money is believed to have come from emergency funding provided by Thames Water's lenders.

The utility company owes roughly Â£20bn and has been working with creditors and government officials to find a way forward.

Failure to reach a deal could lead to Thames Water being forced into a "special administration regime", a form of temporary nationalisation intended to keep the business operating until a viable solution can be found.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has previously said he would like to see "greater public control" of key water and energy utilities.

In the past year, Thames Water boss Chris Weston saw his pay increase 14% to Â£1.63m while other directors received bonuses totalling Â£4.1m.

Speaking on the BBC Big Boss interview late last month, Weston acknowledged there was anger about Thames Water pay, but argued that the company needed to be able attract "capable people to help turn this company around".

"If we're not prepared to pay market rates, then they won't come to us and they won't stay with us," he said.

News.title: Ban on 'subscription traps' brought forward by three months
News.content:
Subscriptions will be easier to cancel and companies will be compelled to make it clear when contracts auto-renew at a higher price, Andy Burnham has announced.

The prime minister is also planning to outlaw shops from falsely claiming products previously retailed at much higher prices to advertise supposed deals, which he said tricks shoppers into thinking they are getting better value on purchases.

Burnham will bring forward a package of changes announced under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer to end so-called subscription traps and a crackdown on "pretend prices".

Shadow chancellor Mel Stride branded the measures "reheated" and said the prime minister "has already run out of ideas".

The plans were announced under Sir Keir in April, but are being brought forward by Burnham's government in a bid to give families "room to breathe" amid the high cost of living.

On subscriptions, the government said the changes will mean businesses have "to provide clearer up-front information, regular reminders and a much easier exit to contracts" for customers.

Burnham, who is embarking on a tour of the UK while Parliament is in recess, has promised a series of "everyday fixes" to help people with the cost of living.

He said: "I'm determined to pull every single lever we can to provide people with some room to breathe on the cost of living."

The measures being brought forward are aimed at making it easier for consumers to cancel unwanted subscriptions and stopping people being rolled onto expensive contracts without their knowledge.

They were expected to come into force next spring, but Burnham's government has promised they will now be implemented by January 2027.

When they were announced in April, the government said the plans would save consumers Â£400m a year in total, or up to Â£170 per person.

At the time, the Department for Business and Trade said there are 10 million unwanted, active subscriptions across the UK.

It said that more than 3.5 million people are being "quietly rolled from free or discounted trials into fully costed contracts", while another 1.3 million are caught out by unexpected auto-renewals.

On top of the already planned changes, Burnham is also vowing to end shops' use of "pretend prices". This will stop retailers using "was" prices, made-up discounts or misleading recommended retail prices (RRPs) to highlight deals.

The government will launch a consultation this autumn to decide how the new measures should be implemented.

News.title: Schools in England have new rules on branded uniforms - will the changes save you money?
News.content:
A new law coming into force in September means parents in England should have to buy fewer branded items of school uniform, which the government says will save them money.

From September, uniforms will be limited to three items with a school logo, like a blazer, jumper or sportswear â plus a tie for secondary schools.

Schools are already advised to keep these items to a minimum, meaning many are already within the rules, but about a quarter of schools will need to make changes by the time the law comes into effect.

The government says the changes will save some families "up to Â£50 per child", but schoolwear suppliers say they now face uncertainty in demand for this year's uniforms.

Co-op Academy Belle Vue, in Manchester, is planning to drop the number of its compulsory branded items from seven to three, plus a tie.

It estimates the average cost of the branded parts of the uniform last year was Â£101.94 with a pinafore, and Â£83.95 without â but this year it will cost families an average of Â£53.97.

Next year, when the school switches to a new supplier, it says it will fall further.

The school has decided to get rid of its branded blazer, the branded pinafore, branded shorts and PE jogging bottoms.

News.title: Fifa and Infantino accused of 'deception' in open letter from football confederations
News.content:
Fifa and its president Gianni Infantino have been accused of breaking trust "through deception" in an open letter issued by Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation.

The letter, signed by the presidents and general secretaries, said recent controversy over the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal was fundamentally about "the integrity of the game, and the integrity of those elected to lead it".

FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, including the World Cups, with 21% sold off to a private investment company.

It was aborted after widespread criticism from several confederations, led by Uefa which has threatened a boycott of all Fifa competitions.

"When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned," the letter read.

It added: "Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding - or demanding - power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it."

While the statement did not name Infantino, sources have told BBC Sport that it should be seen as an opportunity for him to resign and leave his position with dignity.

It comes after Fifa issued a statement on Saturday evening which strongly criticised a "concerted and ongoing effort" to "undermine" the organisation and Infantino.

News.title: Senior detective under investigation over use of AI
News.content:
A senior detective is being investigated over potential artificial intelligence-related gross misconduct.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it had started investigating the officer after they were referred to the watchdog by Derbyshire Police following an "internal review" of their use of AI.

The investigation into the force comes two months after a criminal investigation was launched into another officer accused of using AI systems to "create evidential material in a number of cases".

Derbyshire Police said on Monday it made a voluntary referral to the IOPC on 23 June "regarding an officer's use of artificial intelligence."

The force said the latest investigation was being independently led by the IOPC and it was unable to comment further.

The Financial Times (FT) , external reported that a person familiar with events said the case involved a detective chief inspector at the force alleged to have used AI to maintain "decision logs".

Senior investigators maintain such logs during investigations to record why they took each step, and they can be disclosed for defence lawyers to scrutinise during court cases, the FT said.

News.title: Could your tattoo stop you from getting a job?
News.content:
Tattoos have been in the cultural mainstream for years. Even the prime minister has got one (a bee, on his bicep).

And there are no signs the trend is starting to fade. More people than ever are going under the needle as a form of self-expression: 40% of British 25-49 year-olds have at least one tattoo, according to a 2024 YouGov poll.

The most popular body part to be inked? The upper arm, says YouGov.

But has that acceptance carried over into the workplace?

News.title: Rare £3.7m Ferrari seized in police crackdown
News.content:
A Ferrari valued at about Â£3.7m was among 90 vehicles seized by police during a weekend operation against antisocial driving in central London.

The Metropolitan Police said the vehicles, worth more than Â£8m in total, were taken in Kensington, Chelsea and Hyde Park between Friday and Sunday. Officers targeted uninsured, antisocial and dangerous driving.

The Ferrari Monza SP2 is one of 499 built by the Italian manufacturer and had been in the UK for a day when it was stopped, the force said.

The Met said the driver had been in the car for less than half an hour, held only a provisional licence and had no insurance.

News.title: Risk of patient safety 'bonfire' with Health Bill changes, Lib Dems say
News.content:
The Liberal Democrats have urged Andy Burnham to stop the "bonfire of patient safety" as part of the government's plans to modernise the NHS.

Healthwatch England (HWE), an independent body which represents the views of patients at their local health and social care providers, is set to be scrapped under the NHS Modernisation Bill.

The Health Service Safety Investigation Bureau (HSSIB), which carries out patient safety investigations, is also being abolished.

The government says its changes will strip back bureaucracy and improve patient safety.

The Lib Dems warned it risks another Stafford Hospital scandal â where years of abuse and neglect led to hundreds of unnecessary patient deaths.

A Healthcare Commission report found the scandal â one of the biggest in NHS history â involved at least 400 more deaths than expected between 2005 and 2008.

Under the government proposals, Healthwatch's responsibilities will be transferred to integrated care boards (ICBs) and local authorities, meaning they would have to respond to feedback about their own services, rather than being challenged by an independent body.

Separately, HSSIB's functions will be transferred to the government-run Care Quality Commission (CQC), which the Lib Dems argue raises concerns there is no guarantee that staff who raise safety concerns are given anonymity.

Other measures include the abolition of NHS England in a bid to centralise the running of health and social care services under the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC).

The government says this will reduce bureaucracy and allow more resources to be delivered to frontline healthcare services.

News.title: 'Roll on 2027' as Fleadh 2026 comes to an end
News.content:
The first All Ireland Fleadh in Belfast ended in the early hours of Monday morning with organisers saying they were overwhelmed by the positive response they received from all communities.

It is estimated that there were more than a million people in the city centre during the eight days of the fleadh.

At least 4,000 were still in the grounds of Belfast City Hall at 01:00 BST to hear the closing speeches and final tunes.

Niall McClean, co-chair of the organising committee, told the crowd they were all part of an historic event.

He said: "We've done something that has never, ever happened in this city before. We've brought every single community together â and everybody has absolutely loved it."

McClean added that it has "put a permanent smile on my face. I'm the happiest man in Belfast. Roll on 2027".

"Belfast has shone, the world has come to our doorstep, bringing the biggest numbers ever seen for a Fleadh Cheoil na hÃireann," he said.

The All Ireland Fleadh returns to the city from 1 to 8 August 2027.

News.title: Parents fear being left behind in screening for rare condition after Jesy Nelson campaign
News.content:
Parents of children with a rare genetic condition say they fear Wales is being left behind as other parts of the UK introduce routine screening for newborns.

After widespread campaigning, including by former Little Mix star Jesy Nelson, testing for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) will happen in England and be trialled in Scotland but not in Wales.

Warren Davies, whose three-year-old daughter Ophelia-May has SMA type 2, external, said it felt like the Welsh government was "playing God because they have the opportunity to effect change and are choosing not to".

The Welsh government said it had followed UK National Screening Committee (NSC) guidance that had not recommended routine newborn screening for SMA.

Newborn screening for SMA is also not in place in Northern Ireland, external.

News.title: Banksy works cost public almost £150,000
News.content:
Three artworks by street artist Banksy have cost taxpayers almost Â£150,000 in cleaning operations and security so far, with the bill expected to rise.

The largest single cost relates to a mural painted on the Royal Courts of Justice in September 2025, where removal efforts and security have so far cost more than Â£85,000.

The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) says it has spent Â£50,000 trying to remove paint from the wall of the Grade II-listed building in Carey Street. A further Â£35,300 was spent on overtime and security costs.

The spending was disclosed to the BBC through Freedom of Information requests and is likely to reignite debate over whether Banksy's work is vandalism or valuable public art.

Banksy, who emerged from Bristol's graffiti scene in the 1990s and became one of the world's most famous street artists, is known for murals and installations that often appear overnight and attract large crowds.

The latest costs relate to a mural depicting a judge in a wig battering a protester with his gavel, which appeared on the Royal Courts of Justice in London on 8 September 2025.

Banksy claimed the image as his own work, by posting it on his website and Instagram account.

News.title: Rare turtle to be sent back home in 5,000-mile 'incredibly emotional' trip
News.content:
It has taken almost two years to plan, including building a special temperature-controlled crate for him, and co-ordinating complex paperwork across two countries.

Rhossi normally lives in the sea, but has to travel out of the water â first by helicopter from Anglesey to London, then by cargo flight to Houston, Texas, USA.

It means the journey needs to be completed as quickly as possible, and staff have to be constantly on hand to make sure he does not dry out or dehydrate.

Davidson said: "We have to make sure that the shell is really well lubricated, so we spread Vaseline all over to stop it drying out and flaking off.

"The same for the skin â it's really delicate â and especially the eyes, which both have to be lubricated before he goes into the crate and again just before takeoff, or he will start to peel like someone getting sunburned.

"But I have had to go to the checkout in a chemist's with about eight tubes of KY Jelly and three tubs of Vaseline and explain what's happening when I get strange looks."

News.title: Kellie Bright to leave EastEnders after 13 years
News.content:
EastEnders star Kellie Bright is to leave the soap after playing one of its key characters, Linda Carter, for 13 years.

She arrived in Albert Square with on-screen husband Mick, portrayed by Danny Dyer, when they became the new owners of the Queen Vic pub.

Carter's matriarch character has been central to major storylines including plots about murder, sexual assault and alcoholism.

Bright said she made the "tough decision" to leave more than a year ago but "happily" agreed to stay on to be part of an "exciting storyline".

The BBC has promised "unmissable drama" before her on-screen exit, which is said to be a "while away" yet.

Executive producer Ben Wadey described the actor as being "the beating heart of EastEnders" and said she had become "a classic EastEnders icon".

Viewers have seen the much-loved character at the heart of many emotional storylines including in 2014 when she was raped by her brother-in-law Dean Wicks.

More than 7 million people watched the episode which prompted dozens of complaints. The sexual assault led to long-running story arc about family conflict and trauma.

News.title: Hot weather reveals hidden history across the South
News.content:
As the south of England continues to enjoy an unusually warm and dry summer, parch marks on lawns across the region have revealed the hidden histories of their location.

Among the sites which have seen the outlines of historic installations exposed by the hot weather are Portchester Castle and Blenheim Palace.

At Blenheim, the footprint of an 18th Century garden - which had once stretched across the width of the entire palace - has revealed itself on a lawn.

Andy Mills, the Unesco World Heritage Site's head gardener, told the BBC it was "absolutely magical" to see the outlines of the historic parterre - 260 years after it was demolished.

Mills explained that the original parterre - which is a French word meaning "on the ground" - had been constructed in 1705, and would have "cost an absolute fortune to install".

"It was a very large extravagant thing to do, but it was a way of showing your wealth and importance and that sort of thing," he said.

A record 230 migrants arrived after crossing the Channel to the UK in a single boat on Monday.

The “mega dinghy” left France overnight, arriving in Dover in the early hours. The number breaks the previous record from July when 165 people successfully made the crossing.

Small boats used to cross the Channel have been getting bigger as people smugglers use fewer crossings with more passengers to evade the French authorities.

Small boat crossings to the UK this year are down compared to previous years, with around 14,000 making the journey between January and July.

open image in gallery A deflated dinghy is seen on the quayside in Dover, Kent on Monday. ( PA Wire )

The number of migrants crammed onto a single dinghy has been increasing in recent months, and one dinghy carrying 173 people capsized in the Channel after its engine caught fire earlier in August.

French authorities said that 173 people were rescued by French vessels, helped by two British border force boats and an RNLI lifeboat.

Responding on X on Monday, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said: “At 2.30am this morning a boat carrying 230 people was taken into Dover.

“This is a record number in a single vessel. It’s yet more proof that this illegal invasion is a national security emergency.”

open image in gallery Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Minister for Border Security and Asylum Anna Turley stand by a recovered small boat, used by migrants crossing the English Channel, as he meets with members of the Home Office and the Coastguard, during a visit to HM Coastguard Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre, in Dover, southern England, on August 2, 2026. ( AFP/Getty )

A Home Office spokesperson said: "This latest incident demonstrates the reckless and dangerous tactics employed by the criminal gangs facilitating these crossings, who continue to put lives at risk by cramming ever greater numbers of people onto unseaworthy vessels.

“We are making progress, with the number of small boat crossings down this year and the lowest number recorded for the month of July since 2020.

“But we must go further, which is why we have signed a payment-by-results deal with the French to put 40 per cent more boots on the ground on French beaches.”

open image in gallery People thought to be migrants board a small boat off the coast of Equihen-Plage, France, during an attempt to cross the English Channel in July. ( PA Wire )

Last week, Charlie Eastaugh, director of maritime and small boats at Border Security Command, said that officers were working hard to bring down Channel crossing numbers.

He explained: “It is an active, layered campaign to attack the organised immigration crime model at every stage: upstream, across Europe, in northern France and Belgium, and in the UK.

“The incidents we have seen in the Channel over the last few weeks are a stark reminder of the dangers posed by criminal gangs exploiting people for profit. It is easy to look at out-of-context images and think little is happening to stop these crossings – this is simply not true.

“I know personally how tirelessly French officers have been working to disrupt launches before they reach UK shores. Their efforts include facing violent people with weapons, dispersing huge crowds, arresting smugglers, seizing equipment and collating vital evidence to help our prosecutions – which are at a record high.”

Olivia Attwood has opened up on her “unexpected” romance with radio co-host Pete Wicks.

Attwood, who rose to fame as a contestant on the third series of Love Island in 2017, recently confirmed she was dating Wicks, with whom she presents the Kiss FM radio show The Sunday Roast.

She was previously engaged to footballer Bradley Dack, and they were reported to have married in June 2023; the marriage was not legally binding, though, as the hotel where their wedding was held was not a licensed wedding venue.

Attwood and Dack announced they had separated early this year, with Attwood, 35, confirming in June that she was now dating Wicks, 37.

open image in gallery Pete Wicks and Olivia Attwood in 2025 ( Getty )

Speaking in a new interview with The Times, she revealed: “It was unexpected, we went from platonic to non-platonic very quickly. He’s extremely intelligent and compassionate and patient, all the things I desperately needed but didn’t know I needed.

Suggesting that there were concerns over the speed at which her new relationship was moving, Attwood continued: “Is something amazing happening while I’m still processing something awful? Yes. People are telling me to be single, to go on dates. But if I shut things down with Pete I’d only be dating people to find the connection I have with him.”

Speaking about her desire to have children, she added that she would want them with “the right person”.

“But I could also see it not being part of my story,” she said. “I’m at peace with that. You can’t have everything. So many parts of my life have worked out so much better than I could ever imagine.”

Wicks is another celebrity with a background in reality TV, having risen to fame on the popular reality series The Only Way is Essex.

open image in gallery Bradley Dack and Olivia Attwood in 2025 ( Getty )

Attwood previously addressed her new partner in an interview with Cosmopolitan magazine.

“Once he knew I was separated, he made his feelings known, and it all happened quite quickly,” Attwood said earlier this month.

“It’s the easiest thing I’ve ever done. We’re both in this era where we just want peace and to enjoy life. Personality-wise, I’ve never had a straight man who can go toe-to-toe with me on banter – he is the only one who can keep up.”

“We tick a lot of the boxes that are really important in adult relationships.”

The Burmese military opens fire on anti-government demonstrators, the Syrian army launches a major assault on Beirut, and the United States reveals harrowing evidence of the Srebrenica massacre. Yet somewhere, the sun is still shining. Sort of. As we prepare for our own upcoming eclipse this week, we look back to 1999 when Europe was captivated by two minutes of totality. Meanwhile, a bizarre 2003 blackout brings a different kind of awe to New York, replacing the city lights with a rare, starlit Manhattan sky.

10 August 1988 – Military opens fire on Burmese demonstrators

Security forces in Rangoon fire directly into crowds of peaceful protesters during nationwide demonstrations against dictator Ne Win. The violent clash marked a turning point in the “8888” uprising, which saw thousands of citizens killed across the country. The revolt was ultimately crushed weeks later by a bloody military coup that installed a junta that ruled for decades.

open image in gallery ( The Independent )

14 August 1989 – Syrian army launches major assault on Beirut

Syrian forces unleash a relentless heavy artillery bombardment against Christian enclaves in Beirut, breaching lines held by General Michel Aoun. The violent escalation marked a climax in Aoun’s “War of Liberation”, which aimed to drive Syrian troops out of Lebanon. Although international mediation brokered the historic Taif Agreement months later, the conflict only fully ended in October 1990 when Syrian forces ousted Aoun into exile.

open image in gallery ( The Independent )

14 August 1990 – US faces pushback over unilateral Gulf blockade

The US finds itself diplomatically isolated after launching a unilateral naval interdiction to choke off Iraqi oil exports and imports. European allies including Britain initially refused to join the pre-emptive operation without a clear international mandate. The rift proved temporary, as the UN Security Council soon approved Resolution 665, uniting an unprecedented global coalition that eventually launched Operation Desert Storm.

open image in gallery ( The Independent )

11 August 1995 – Evidence exposes mass atrocities in Srebrenica

The US reveals harrowing eyewitness testimonies and spy photos to the UN demonstrating that Bosnian Serb forces executed thousands of Muslim men and boys. The compelling body of evidence stripped away remaining doubts about the scale of the massacre. The mounting outrage over these exposed horrors broke diplomatic deadlocks, directly triggering a decisive Nato military intervention weeks later.

open image in gallery ( The Independent )

12 August 1996 – Oasis play iconic concerts at Knebworth Park

Oasis perform to massive crowds across two nights at Knebworth Park in what becomes a defining live event of the 1990s Britpop era. Millions of fans applied for tickets in an unprecedented rush that represented the greatest demand for a concert in British history and shattered attendance records for the largest open-air rock concerts held in the country.

open image in gallery ( The Independent )

12 August 1999 – Total solar eclipse of 1999

Millions of people across Europe stop to marvel as the moon perfectly blocks out the sun in a stunning two-minute celestial display. The highly anticipated event marked the first total solar eclipse visible from the United Kingdom since 1927. The spectacle remains a rare memory since the UK will not see another total eclipse until 2090.

open image in gallery ( The Independent )

16 August 2003 – Blackout brings Manhattan to a standstill

A massive power outage shuts down New York City and the wider northeast, bringing traffic to a halt but allowing rare starlight to shine above Manhattan. While the abrupt blackout had raised immediate fears of another coordinated terror attack after 9/11, the true cause was revealed to be a single overgrown tree in Ohio that brushed against a sagging high-voltage power line.

open image in gallery ( The Independent )

13 August 2008 – End of Russo-Georgian war

A resurgent Russia halts its swift military offensive against Georgia after sweeping into the breakaway region of South Ossetia and advancing deep into undisputed territory. The brief but brutal war left hundreds dead and forcibly displaced tens of thousands of civilians before European diplomats successfully brokered a fragile ceasefire agreement. The crushing Russian victory signalled the definitive return of aggressive great power politics.

The European Union is considering further delaying the full rollout of its entry/exit system (EES) in order to avoid added complications at its borders, according to a report.

The EU finally introduced its new border security system in stages from October last year, replacing the old process of manually stamping passports with the registration of biometric details when travellers arrive in Europe.

But the system has already faced calls to be scrapped after creating bottlenecks at airports, with a fifth of Brits now considering cancelling their European holidays this summer due to the chaos.

Industry sources told The Times that Apostolos Tzitzikostas, the commissioner responsible for negotiations over the EES with non-EU countries, has privately assured the checks will be paused.

open image in gallery Airlines warn many airports do not yet have enough biometric scanners and staff to facilitate the EES system, creating delays ( Getty/iStock )

Mr Tzitzikostas was said to be pushing to extend a derogation allowing officials to suspend the new checks past the existing deadline of 6 September for the full rollout.

And he was reported to have already made assurances to the UK that an extension is possible, having recently. met with transport secretary Heidi Alexander, according to the newspaper.

The department said last month that Ms Alexander had raised concerns about the EU’s new digital border check system with Mr Tzitzikostas during their meeting on 14 July.

Ms Alexander said in a statement at the time: “We want everyone to have the summer holidays they deserve – and yesterday’s meeting shows everyone is pulling in the same direction.

“I was reassured that the EU commissioner for transport understood the concerns of holidaymakers and recognised the need for us to work together.”

That came amid reports that passengers were missing their flights due to long queues, while Ryanair warned of “queue chaos” from the new system, which it said was not ready for full implementation.

open image in gallery Apostolos Tzitzikostas, pictured here last year, reportedly gave his representations to Heidi Alexander when they met on 14 July ( AFP/Getty )

They pointed to several popular airports including Spain’s Alicante, which they said was not ready for the checks due to “insufficient staff, kiosks and system readiness”.

Alicante-Elche Miguel Hernández airport is now preparing for a £985 million upgrade including facilities to streamline EES checks.

The EU's EES only became fully operational in April and applies to all 29 Schengen countries, most of which are EU member states, with further operations expected in the autumn.

The system requires travellers to register their biometric details, such as fingerprints and a photo, when they arrive in the EU, replacing the previous system of manually stamping passports.

EES is required for all non-EU passengers entering or exiting Schengen countries.

The British government has announced £20 million in new funding to increase the number of booths for passport checks at the country's main gateway to Europe, the Port of Dover.

The majority of the new checks will be done in EU member states, but will take place in Britain for those using the ferry through the Port of Dover or taking the train into the EU, the government said.

The boss of John Lewis, Peter Ruis, is set to step down from the department store chain.

He will be replaced by Will Kernan, the former boss of high street retailers River Island and The White Company.

Parent group the John Lewis Partnership said Mr Ruis will step down as managing director of the John Lewis business in September.

The company said the boss is stepping away from the retail chain “to pursue new projects”.

open image in gallery John Lewis has 36 shops across the UK (Tony Buckingham/John Lewis/PA) ( PA Media )

Mr Ruis has led the brand through its major turnaround programme since January 2024, having rejoined the group where he had earlier been a buying director.

He also led the reintroduction of the brand’s Never Knowingly Undersold price promise and has overseen the start of an £800 million store investment plan.

His replacement will now be tasked with helping John Lewis Partnership chairman Jason Tarry with returning the group to profit despite a challenging consumer backdrop.

Mr Kernan currently sits on the John Lewis Partnership board as a non-executive director and will take up the managing director role in “mid-September”, ahead of the peak trading period in the run-up to Christmas.

Mr Ruis said: “After nearly three years of significant investment and modernisation, the business is now on a much stronger footing.

“I’m so proud of what we’ve achieved and there is so much more still to come.

“I would like to thank our customers, partners, brands and suppliers for their incredible support and I wish Will the best of luck as he takes up the reins.”

Mr Kernan said: “Having served on the partnership’s board for three years, I have a clear understanding of the John Lewis business and a huge appreciation for the partnership’s values and employee-ownership model.

“We have significant headroom for growth and I’m looking forward to leading the team to ensure John Lewis remains the country’s most trusted and loved retailer, in store and online.”

News.content:

Keely Hodgkinson returns to competition at the European Athletics Championships in an unusual position. After breaking the world indoor record over 800m in March, it looked as though the world was at her feet. But the Paris Olympic champion has had a distinctly stop-start outdoor season, troubled by a “freak” injury and dogged by bad luck, and has been beaten resoundingly, twice, by Switzerland’s breakout star Audrey Werro, the fastest woman in the world this year.

With that in mind, does she still believe she is the best in the world, going into a major championships on home soil? On a video call with The Independent and other outlets, she smiles confidently as she says: “Yes, I still believe I’m very much capable of that.

“This is what I trained for, this is the exciting moment. I’ve been doing this for a couple of years now, had lots of people come around and challenge me, and I’ve always been there. I’m proud to have always been in that top segment, I’ve medalled at every single championships. So it’s really great to have the women’s 800 in the spotlight and everyone getting behind us and wanting us to run fast, it’s really exciting.”

The 24-year-old’s outdoor woes began when she fell in training onto a metal grate that left her with cuts to her knees before the Prefontaine Classic in Oregon, where she lost to world champion Lilian Odira. She suffered surprise back-to-back defeats and withdrew in tears from the British national championships earlier this summer, moments before the 400m final, after tweaking her hamstring.

Now she is relaxed about the fall; her knees have healed – “I’ve got some fat scars, but they’re all fine” – and the incident didn’t cause her to miss any training. “It was like, how much pain can I manage? Against these girls, if you’re limping and your back’s out, all these little fine margins can affect your performance.

open image in gallery Hodgkinson returned to winning ways at the London Diamond League last month ( Getty )

“I just fell over, it’s a freak accident, who cares? I think people are very quick to judge and don’t really fully know what has happened. I wanted to run, I was there, I flew all the way out. Maybe in hindsight I probably shouldn’t have, but, I was there, I just thought, why not?”

She returned to winning ways on home soil at the London Diamond League last month, but cannot be considered the out-and-out favourite – although she remains a major force – in a glittering field.

Switzerland’s Werro has been the surprise package of the season and is the outright favourite after running the fastest times in the world this year. She won the Diamond League in Stockholm in one minute 53.98 seconds – the third fastest women’s 800m ever and the quickest this year – to leave Hodgkinson a distant second, even with a new personal best and British record time of 1:54.33.

Hodgkinson reflected on that race, saying: “I didn’t know what she was capable of at that point, and I think that just shows you that you can’t underestimate anybody. If you look at all our other head-to-heads, you wouldn’t have thought she was going to hang on. I don’t think I did anything wrong – I think people were trying to make me feel like it was a failure and it really wasn’t. That was a British record, it was my fastest time ever, and I’m going to remind myself of that because I’m proud of that.”

open image in gallery It has been a stop-start season for the Brit who withdrew from the national championships in tears ( PA Wire )

Hodgkinson has become used to being the athlete to beat throughout her young career, a generational talent who wins with ease. This year she has been on the back foot. With Femke Broeders-Bol – having converted her brilliance in her normal discipline of 400m hurdles to the 800m – also a potent force, the 800 is set to be the race of the championships, but it may not go all Hodgkinson’s way.

She is taking a relaxed approach to that. “I’ve obviously got a lot of experience, and experience can be both a positive and a negative thing. Sometimes you overthink more because it’s like, I’ve done it this way, I’ve done it this way. So I just like to go back to basics, like when I was young, upcoming, I didn’t care. I had nothing to lose and I think it’s important for me that I hold on to that and I just race with courage and fearlessness and I think that’s how I’ll get the best out of myself.”

Of the strength of her competition, she says: “I think it definitely just helps motivation-wise. This is what I love about championships. I’ve gone into them ranked eighth in the Olympics in Tokyo, came out with a silver; I’ve gone in as favourite and not won. I think it’s like a bit of a clean slate.

“The standard now in Europe has gone up [over the last few years], so I think the heats, the semis are going to be a lot faster than what we’ve seen in the last couple of years. It does mean you’ve got to bring your A game a bit sooner. But I think that’s a bit better for me because I like to line up and feel like, you know, this matters, I’m gonna have to run fast, I’ve got these girls to run against. I think it’s really exciting, the levels that we have.”

open image in gallery She was part of a trio of British success stories at the world indoor championships in Poland ( Getty )

She had initially pencilled in the London Diamond League for an attempt at breaking the infamous world outdoor record, having smashed the world indoor record in March. But it now looks as though Werro, who became the first woman since the controversial Jarmila Kratochvilova to run under 1:54 – twice – in Paris and Stockholm this year, is the best placed to finally topple the Czech’s mark of 1:53.28, which has stood since 1983.

The stage is set for a hugely entertaining race – the only drawback is that newly crowned Commonwealth 800m champion Georgia Hunter Bell is opting not to compete over the distance in Birmingham, focusing on the 1,500m instead.

Hunter Bell and Hodgkinson are training partners and close friends, but the 32-year-old has spoken openly about her desire to double up, racing both the 800m and 1,500m, in future championships, adding yet another rivalry to the 800m field and another dynamic to negotiate for coaches Trevor Painter and Jenny Meadows.

open image in gallery Training partners and rivals Hodgkinson and Georgia Hunter Bell will not compete over the same distance in Birmingham ( PA Wire )

Asked whether she would relish the challenge of having another rival over 800m, Hodgkinson says: “If Georgia wants to do that, that doesn’t really affect me. I think it’d be great. Obviously we train together, we push each other really hard, we’re both in really good shape. When we plan our races, I sit down with Trevor and plan mine, she does hers and whatever she feels like she wants to do.

“I think with there being three championships [UK nationals, Commonwealths and Europeans] and her being decisive between the two events, she’s just done what is best for her. But I’m sure there’ll be a time this season that we do match up and it’ll be a good race.”

She laughs as she recalls something the pair recently saw on social media about their rivalry, real or imagined: “Me and Georgia were laughing the other day because we saw a TikTok, and it was like: ‘Georgia pays Keely 200k to not do the Commonwealth Games.’ I thought, well I didn’t get that money, so where the fuck’s it gone? But I don’t know. People make up stuff. We just laugh about it.”

News.title: Thailand gunman calls TV presenter live on air after government office shooting
News.content:
A gunman called a Thai TV host during a live broadcast and admitted to shooting at a local government office in Nonthaburi province on Monday (10 August).

Thongchai Yenprasert, the president of the Nonthaburi Provincial Administrative Organisation, died in hospital while receiving treatment after he was shot multiple times, according to officials.

A well-known former lawmaker, Chalong Reawraeng, has claimed responsibility for the attack.

He first claimed it in a phone call to Anchalee Paireerak, a popular political commentator, who was livestreaming on YouTube at the time. The presenter said on the livestream: “You just shot him just now? Is he dead? Did he die?

“Don't go anywhere, you have to wait there for the police, don't move around."

Viewers were not able to hear the caller.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want
News.content:
Liverpool 2 Monaco 3

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

News.title: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
News.content:
Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s pre-season woes are a sign of what’s to come if Declan Rice and Co aren’t back sooner rather than later
Sports.content:
ARSENAL’S pre-season struggles are a warning sign for what might happen if their World Cup stars are not back sharpish.

And the Gunners will be desperate to get new £75m signing Bruno Guimaraes ready for action as soon as possible to make things right.



The reigning champions have leaked six goals in two consecutive pre-season defeats as Mikel Arteta battles to manage his bare-bones squad.

Sunday afternoon’s 3-2 defeat to Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium marked the first time since April 2023 that Arsenal conceded three or more goals in consecutive games.



It followed their 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday and will have alarm bells ringing for Arteta with the Community Shield just SIX days away.

Arsenal kick off their campaign proper with a trip to Cardiff this Sunday, taking on Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City in the annual curtain raiser.



City have dispatched teams like Atletico Madrid in pre-season and are already playing with top returning players like Antoine Semenyo and Omar Marmoush.

But Arteta finds himself without a host of top stars, which has made his champions look like a shadow of their usual selves in pre-season.

England quartet Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke and Ebere Eze, and world champions Mikel Merino, David Raya and Martin Zubimendi will only begin their pre-season preparations today.

Martin Odegaard played just 30 minutes against Dortmund after returning to training last week, and he will need more minutes in the tank before he can be trusted to play a full game.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Meanwhile Jurrien Timber and William Saliba both remain out with groin and back injuries, respectively, and are not expected to return for the start of the season.

The absence of those players has been felt throughout Arsenal’s pre-season.

Yesterday’s defeat to Dortmund showed Arsenal’s defensive frailties when Saliba and Timber are unavailable.



Cristhian Mosquera fell asleep, allowing Samuele Inacio to ghost in behind him and score the opener for Dortmund.

And Arsenal finished the game with 18-year-old prospect Theo Julienne at right-back after Ben White was substituted – showing their lack of depth in that position without Timber.

Arteta revealed after the game that both Timber and Saliba are still some way from returning to the fold.

The Arsenal boss said: “Jurrien is progressing really well. He’s on the pitch, he’s doing quite a lot right now. But he’s still weeks away. I cannot tell you how much.

“And William is in rest mode at the moment for two weeks. He had to do almost nothing, don’t aggravate the injury. It’s going to take some time to heal. We know that.”



In midfield, Myles Lewis-Skelly has been operating out-of-position as a lone No6.

Given his inexperience in that area, attacking players have run riot around him without an experienced head to help him through the game.

That was evidenced when Konstantino Karetsas stormed through Arsenal’s midfield as if it didn’t exist before firing a curling effort in for Dortmund’s second goal.



Guimaraes, who was paraded out on the pitch before kick-off, can be the man to help solve that problem when Arsenal take on City on Sunday – but only if he is ready in time.

Arteta will be desperately scrambling to integrate the Brazilian into training and get him up to scratch during their final pre-season friendly against Como on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham was watching from the stands too, at the Emirates to support his brother Jobe who started in midfield for Dortmund.

And what Arteta would give to have a superstar like him available to command the middle of the park in the absence of Rice and Zubimendi.

The Arsenal duo haven’t kicked a ball since the World Cup, and their return seems unlikely before Sunday’s Community Shield.



However, Arteta said that some of his World Cup returnees could be put on a fast track back to action if they were used sparingly during the summer tournament.

He added: “We have very different groups within the same time that they are coming back.

“Some of them, they’ve done more. Others, they’ve done less. Some of them, they almost didn’t participate in the World Cup in terms of minutes. So they are all very different stages.”



There are still some positives in the performance of new addition Christos Tzolis, who continued his pre-season form by getting an assist and winning a penalty.

But it feels paramount that Arteta gets some of his stars back as soon as possible, with Arsenal facing a monstrous start to the season.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Gunners take on Man City, Coventry, Aston Villa and Chelsea in a tricky start to their title defence.

If they have to face those challenges without their best players back in action, they could hit a stumbling block or two – leaving them playing catch-up in the title race.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland becomes a tourist attraction as boat full of cheering people sails past his yacht while he’s on holiday
Sports.content:
ERLING HAALAND was stunned after a boat full of adoring fans gatecrashed his holiday.

The Manchester City striker, 26, has been relaxing following a World Cup to remember.



Haaland bagged seven goals before Norway’s dream run was ended by England in the quarter-finals.

And the lethal finisher jetted out to Sicily to soak up the sun ahead of the new Premier League season.



But Haaland appears to have become a tourist attraction after a boat full of cheering people pulled up alongside his luxury yacht to get a glimpse of him in the flesh.

The fans also raced to get photos of Haaland, whose number of Instagram followers skyrocketed during the World Cup, before sailing away.

Footage of the incident has gone viral since being uploaded onto YouTube and social media.

In the video, the City favourite said: “They do tourist boats. Go and drive past where Haaland stays.



“Come have a look at where Erling Haaland stays. I’ve never seen anything like it.”

The former Borussia Dortmund man boarded the yacht after heading to team-mate Gianluigi Donnarumma’s wedding last month – where he hilariously led a Viking Row.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And Haaland turned into a jealous boyfriend when partner Isabel Johansen was seen chatting to Italian actor Michele Morrone.

But the marksman’s time away from the pitch is coming to an end because he is due to return to City ahead of the Community Shield showdown with Arsenal on Sunday.



It is the first time Haaland will be available since Enzo Maresca replaced Pep Guardiola in the Etihad Stadium dugout.

City have locked horns with European heavyweights Inter Milan and Atletico Madrid during preparations for the new season.

The Sky Blues also notched a comfortable win over the K League All-Stars during their Asia tour.



Haaland and Co will get their Premier League title push underway with a clash against Bournemouth on August 23.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino accused of ‘breaking trust through deception’ as Uefa and other football bosses pen furious letter
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO has been accused of “breaking trust through deception” in a damning letter from football bosses.

Uefa and their Asian and North American counterparts, the AFC and Concacaf, teamed up to pen the furious statement taking aim at the Fifa president.



Infantino has come under heavy fire since his controversial plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

He made an embarrassing U-turn and ditched his money-grabbing scheme in a desperate attempt to cling on to his power and position.



Uefa and the other confederations were willing to boycott the World Cup and have even started discussions to launch rival tournaments to “paralyse Fifa”.

And now they have co-signed the letter which directly hits out at Infantino’s leadership.



The lengthy post – entitled an “open letter to the football family” – was signed by the Uefa, AFC and Concacaf presidents and general secretaries, including Aleksander Ceferin.

It says: “This is about something more fundamental: the integrity of the game, and the integrity of those elected to lead it.

“Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held.

“It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.

“Fifa’s recent letter to its Vice-Presidents and 211 Member Associations acknowledges that mistakes were made in the process.

“It treats this as a failure of communication, when what football witnessed was a failure of judgment.

“A proposal advanced on a compressed timeline, without meaningful consultation, and pushed toward a deadline before Member Associations could properly review its terms is not the product of an oversight — it is the product of a design intended to limit scrutiny.



“It did not acknowledge that the proposal itself was inherently wrong.

“There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the Fifa World Cup was a profound failure of judgment — not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions Fifa exists to serve.”

The letter also called for an independent commission to conduct the review into Fifa’s recent conduct – not an internal Fifa committee.

It went on to point out that only one election official was part of the Fifa crisis meeting in Morocco last week – with no Fifa Council members or member associations invited to contribute.

The letter continued: “This recent meeting, where a select number of members of the Fifa Management Committee—not the full Committee—were summoned abroad, rather than leadership going to Zurich to address the heart of Fifa, its staff, only reinforces these concerns and

represents a continuation of the very pattern of conduct that brought us to this moment.



“It is not the conduct of a custodian of the game, but of one who believes the game is answerable to him.

“There is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness.

“These are not the qualities football deserves in its leadership.

“That is why we have taken this stance: not lightly and not alone, but together, and out of duty to the game we serve.

“Football’s strength has always been its unity. We call for that unity to be honoured now, for leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it.”



SunSport understands Concacaf, Uefa and the AFC are pressurising Infantino to resign with immediate effect and not run for re-election in March.

LaLiga chief Javier Tebas, meanwhile, insists the Infantino era is “over” and he is “destroying the very essence of football”.

Tebas fumed in an interview with Le Monde: “For me, Gianni Infantino’s time has long since passed.

“Gianni Infantino is not someone who contributes to the growth of football.

“On the contrary, his projects are destroying the very essence of the sport: the national leagues.



“Football is not limited to the elite. For me, the Infantino era is over.

“What remains to be seen is when that will take effect and how the succession will unfold.

“I hope it is not just a matter of swapping out some people for others, but of a genuine overhaul.”

As well as the scandalous attempt to privatise the World Cup, it has also been revealed in bombshell documents that Infantino was actually plotting to partner with the rebel breakaway European Super League – and it could even have been called the Fifa Super League.

Also, The Telegraph reported on Friday that Uefa paid off a six-figure sum to an alleged mistress of married Infantino while he was general secretary.

And SunSport revealed his latest blow that even his hometown club Zug 94 in Switzerland are refusing to back his beleaguered leadership.

Sports.title: Amanda Staveley ‘wants to buy London Stadium at bargain price’ if she lands stake in West Ham
Sports.content:
AMANDA STAVELEY wants to buy the London Stadium if she becomes a major West Ham shareholder.

The British business executive is reportedly keen on exploring a bargain deal for the Hammers’ home if her bid for David Gold’s family’s 25 per cent stake is successful.



Staveley, 53, is locked in a boardroom battle with current co-owner Daniel Kretinsky, who is also trying to land the shares.

But if she comes out on top, her ambitions may not stop at buying into the Championship club.



According to The Times, Staveley wants to look at buying the London Stadium from the Greater London Authority.

And London mayor Sir Sadiq Khan has opened the door to talks if a sale could save taxpayers money.

A spokesman for Khan said: “The Mayor would welcome any discussions regarding the London Stadium that would deliver greater value for money for Londoners.”

The stadium – built for the 2012 Olympics – is thought to be worth as little as £50MILLION because of the huge cost of running it.

West Ham‘s favourable tenancy agreement after moving into the stadium in 2016 has long been criticised, with the deal regularly labelled the “deal of the century”.

The Hammers were paying around £4.4m a season to use the ground while they were in the Premier League, but that fee has now been cut following relegation.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Meanwhile, the latest accounts are expected to show the stadium is costing taxpayers around £19m to operate.

Any sale would still come with strings attached, with London’s bid to host the 2029 World Athletics Championships meaning any MAJOR redevelopment would likely have to wait until after the event.

Staveley – who pulled the strings in the Saudi takeover of Newcastle – hinted at those wider ambitions in an interview with Bloomberg last week, saying: “Whatever club we take, there’ll be a big property play as well.

“We won’t just do a football-led.



“I just want a challenge, and that’s what excites me.

“That’s where you get value uplift – when you take something from seedling and allow it to grow.”

But before she can start thinking about the stadium, Staveley first has to win the battle for a stake in West Ham.

Staveley’s improved bid for the Gold family’s 25 per cent shareholding has been accepted.

BUT Kretinsky – who owns 27 per cent already – has first refusal on the shares and is trying to get a deal over the line himself.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy could make sensational return to English football as West Ham ‘keep eye on transfer situation’
Sports.content:
WEST HAM are reportedly considering a shock move for Jamie Vardy in their desperate push for more firepower.

The Hammers are targeting an immediate return to the Premier League after being relegated to the Championship last season.



And they made a winning start to their competitive campaign after seeing off Portsmouth in the first round of the Carabao Cup on Saturday.

But West Ham boss Nuno Espirito Santo is still in the market for a striker in the final weeks of the transfer window.



Sky Sports report the Hammers are keeping an eye on Vardy’s situation after his exit from Italian side Cremonese.

The one-time Premier League champion, 39, is a free agent following his decision to quit.

Vardy failed to avoid the drop from Serie A despite notching seven goals in 29 appearances last term.

And West Ham are showing interest in offering him a route back into English football.

Taty Castellanos, who bagged a brace in the win over Portsmouth, is the East Londoners’ first-choice frontman.

Pablo is still searching for his first goal since joining West Ham in a £21.8million move from Gil Vicente in January.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Niclas Fullkrug has brutally been left without a squad number following his return from a loan spell at AC Milan.

Vardy made himself a Premier League legend during his 13-year spell with Leicester.

He spearheaded the Foxes to their shock title win in the 2015/16 season and scored 145 goals in 342 top flight appearances.

The former England marksman would also head to West Ham with Championship pedigree, having clinched promotion from the second tier twice.



Vardy’s arrival would come after Joel Veltman became the Hammers’ first summer addition last week.

West Ham get their Championship campaign underway with a trip to Burnley on Sunday.

Sports.title: Brighton team preview: top stars, smart options & potential flops
Sports.content:
BRIGHTON players will be considerably more popular in Dream Team this season if they win their Conference League play-off.

English clubs have dominated Uefa’s tertiary competition since its inception in 2022 with West Ham, Chelsea and Crystal Palace all lifting the trophy in the last four years.

PLAY DREAM TEAM NOW: £100,000 PRIZE POT!



The addition of favourable European commitments will put the Seagulls firmly in the sights of crafty Dream Team bosses.



Here we have analysed the top stars, smart options and potential flops in Fabian Hurzeler’s squad.

TOP STARS

Yankuba Minteh (£4m) is the exact type of player who might capitalise on a Thursday night when Brighton are up against a team difficult to pinpoint on a map — see Ismaila Sarr last season.

The 22-year-old winger has talent to burn and while his end product still needs refining, he’s a potential matchwinner whenever he steps onto the pitch.

Minteh limped off during a pre-season win over Roma at the weekend but Hurzeler remained optimistic when questioned on the incident after the game.

Elsewhere, Bart Verbruggen (£4m) is a fantastic goalkeeper worthy of an increased price tag in 2026/27.

The Netherlands international enhanced his reputation at the World Cup with some sharp saves and is said to be courted by some big European clubs.



If he stays at the Amex he will be hopeful of a sizeable clean sheet tally — only Arsenal and Manchester City conceded fewer home league goals than Brighton in 2025/26.

Those defensive numbers also improve Ferdi Kadioglu’s (3.5m) viability.

The Turkish left-back was voted Brighton’s Player of the Year in May, a reflection of his work rate and tactical awareness.

Truth be told, Kadioglu is yet to truly light up Dream Team but those who watch him regularly will agree he’s capable of useful returns.

SMART OPTIONS

Pascal Gross (£3.5m) ticks a lot of boxes.

A clever, well-rounded footballer, the German midfielder has several routes to points: tackles, bonus points, big chances created and assists.

His goal threat has diminished in recent years so gaffers shouldn’t expect mega hauls but he’s a reliable, affordable asset who tends to tick over — a steady hand for the first two or three months of the campaign.

Gross is now 35 years old so it’s understandable if Dream Team bosses are a tad reluctant but Hurzeler knows better than anyone that the fan favourite’s return from Borussia Dortmund was a decisive factor in propelling the Seagulls away from the relegation scrap to European qualification.



Plus, he’s a regular set-piece taker and may even be on penalties.

On the other end of the experience scale, 19-year-old Luka Vuskovic (£3.5m) is a player to monitor closely.

The young centre-back scored 13 league goals across the last two seasons while on loan at Westerlo and Hamburg — goal-scoring defenders are worth their weight in gold in Dream Team.

There is a slight concern about Vuskovic’s playing time but the fact Brighton forked out a club-record fee to sign him from Tottenham suggests he is viewed as Jan Paul van Hecke’s successor.



Gaffers should keep an eye on Stefanos Tzimas’ (£2.5m) progress.

The Greek striker suffered an ACL rupture last season but it wouldn’t be a surprise if he got his fair share of minutes now Danny Welbeck has departed for Chelsea.

His price will look extraordinarily cheap if he is given a run of starts, which certainly isn’t unthinkable.

POTENTIAL FLOPS

Georginio Rutter (£3.5m) is one of the most entertaining players in the Premier League but Dream Team managers must apply a cold, analytical approach.



The talented Frenchman is categorised as a striker – a role he fulfilled more often that not last season – but the general consensus is that he’s more effective as a No10.

For all his invention and creativity, Rutter is not a natural goalscorer and so it’s hard to justify his selection as a forward in the world of Dream Team.

We would love to be proved wrong but at this stage we have concerns about Kaoru Mitoma (£4m).

The Japanese winger is expected to miss the start of the campaign as he continues to recover from the injury that ruled him out of the World Cup.

Our main concern is that he hasn’t been able to replicate the form he exhibited in the second half of the 2024/25 season, when he was a relatively popular selection amid a flurry of goal involvements.
