Sports.title: Bradley Barcola ‘gives green light’ for transfer as Arsenal set to battle Liverpool for £130m PSG star
Sports.content:
BRADLEY BARCOLA has reportedly given the green light to Liverpool amid interest from Arsenal in the PSG star.

Barcola – valued at around £130million – has become one of the most coveted players of the summer.



Liverpool and Arsenal have emerged as the two leading favourites for his signature.

But the Reds looked to have edged ahead of the Gunners after getting the thumbs up from Barcola on personal terms, according to Fabrizio Romano.



Liverpool remain in negotiations with PSG over a fee, the report says.

But it claims getting the deal done will be “up to Liverpool” because PSG’s valuation “remains high” at £130m.



New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola is keen to get a new winger over the line after losing Mo Salah on a free transfer.

But Arsenal are eager to strengthen on the wing too after Leandro Trossard joined Besiktas.

And Mikel Arteta has also been forced to move on from Vinicius Jr after the club’s ambitious move for the Real Madrid star quickly collapsed.

But they face an uphill battle to get the upper hand on Barcola given Liverpool had a headstart.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But Liverpool still haven’t agreed a fee with PSG, which could allow Arsenal back into the race.

French outlet Canal Plus reported that Liverpool didn’t have the means to match their sky-high price and the transfer tug-of-war is far from over.

Barcola, 23, has played 152 times for the French giants since joining from Lyon in 2023, scoring 39 goals and contributing towards two Champions Leagues and three Ligue 1 titles.

But he has struggled to nail down a regular first team spot amid competition with Ousmane Dembele, Desiree Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.



Liverpool have already brought in winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna but will be after more options amid doubt over Cody Gakpo’s future.

Arsenal recently snapped up Newcastle talisman Bruno Guimaraes for around £75m but Arteta will need more attacking reinforcements as he bids to defend his title.

Arsenal admire Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez, but a deal will be very difficult to accomplish.

Another option is Everton ace Iliman Ndiaye.

Sports.title: Super League's Final Charge: Play-off spots taking shape with five rounds left
Sports.content:
There are just five rounds of Super League action remaining and, with it, a whole lot of drama as Super League's Final Charge ramps up.

Seven teams remain in contention for a play-off spot and most of those are still eyeing a top-two finish.

In Super League, the two teams who finish in first and second are guaranteed a home semi-final across Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26.

In the week prior to that, the Play-Off Eliminators occur in which the third-place team takes on the team in sixth and fourth plays fifth for the chance to make it into the semis.

Then the winners of the semi-finals head to the Grand Final at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3.

There are going to be so many twists and turns along the way and you can catch them all live on Sky Sports.

With that in mind, let's take a look at what each team has remaining and what is on the line for them...

1) Leeds Rhinos (36 points)

Leeds Rhinos have been sitting pretty at the summit of Super League for a while now and they will want to hold onto that for their five remaining fixtures.

They stayed top in spectacular fashion with a win over Wakefield Trinity in their latest game, showing they mean business.

They last won the League Leaders' Shield way back in 2015 and last won a trophy in 2020 when they took Challenge Cup glory, so finishing top would see a welcome return of some silverware for the Rhinos.

In their last five matches, they face Leigh Leopards (H), York Knights (A), St Helens (A), Wigan Warriors (A) and Hull FC (H).

That means they have three teams in their run-in who are hunting play-off places. If they can remain unbeaten, League Leaders' Shield glory will be theirs and they will be one match from walking out at the 'Theatre of Dreams' once again.

2) Wigan Warriors (34 points)

The team who have been there, done that, and got the T-shirt. Matt Peet, head coach of Wigan, has made no secret of how hard he is pushing for a top-two finish because he knows how crucial that home semi-final is.

Not only that, the Warriors will be hungry to avenge their Grand Final defeat to Hull KR in 2025.

They have the Challenge Cup in their trophy cabinet and will have all eyes on adding a second piece of silverware.

Ahead of the play-offs, they still have to play Bradford Bulls (A), Wakefield Trinity (H), Hull KR (H), Leeds Rhinos (A) and Catalans Dragons (H).

Wigan are likely to have their sights firmly set on ensuring they beat Wakefield and Leeds to pile on the pressure.

3) Wakefield Trinity (32 points)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Caius Faatili produced an incredible run as he set up Caleb Hamlin-Uele's try for Wakefield against Leeds

What a season it has been for Wakefield Trinity. They are on the hunt for their highest Super League finish, but will now want to bounce back following their heart-breaking two-point defeat to top-of-the-table Leeds.

Wakefield returned to Super League last year following their relegation in 2024 and have lit up the competition, their star-studded side becoming a formidable one.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Sinfield scored for Wakefield against his father's former side Leeds as rugby league legend Kevin watched on proudly

They have games against St Helens (H), Wigan Warriors (A), York Knights (H), Warrington Wolves (H) and Leigh Leopards (A) left. That is four teams out of the seven still in the fight.

They will look at York as an absolute must-win and crucial two points. The Wigan and Warrington games will also be key as they are two other teams right in the chase for a top-two spot.

4) Warrington Wolves (30 points, one game in hand)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League clash between Bradford Bulls and Warrington Wolves as Matty Ashton scored twice in a dominant 42-4 victory for the visitors

Warrington Wolves, along with Hull KR, have six matches remaining thanks to their rescheduled round-two match.

This was moved due to the Robins playing in Las Vegas.

With that, it is a more jam-packed Final Charge for them but also one gives Sam Burgess' side a good opportunity to prosper.

In their remaining fixtures, they face York Knights (H), Hull KR (A), Huddersfield Giants (H), Hull FC (A), Wakefield Trinity (A) and Toulouse Olympique (H).

If the Wolves are going to be contenders, they will have to pick up points against the four lowly sides they face.

5) Hull KR (28 points, one game in hand)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Castleford Tigers against Hull KR from the Super League

The other side with six games remaining, Hull KR, are right in the mix and will want it to stay that way and climb as high up the table as possible.

The Robins were the team who did it all in 2025, ending the wait for a new team to win the competition, and now they will want to send coach Willie Peters out on a high by going back to back.

Their remaining six matches are against Catalans Dragons (H), Warrington Wolves (H), Toulouse Olympique (H), Wigan Warriors (A), Huddersfield Giants (H) and St Helens (A).

Four out of the six are at Craven Park, which will only boost their chances. Wins against Catalans, Toulouse and Huddersfield will also be a non-negotiable.

6) Leigh Leopards (28 points)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Leigh Leopards against York Knights from the Super League

The team that has become renowned for coming good when they need to, Leigh Leopards want to shore up their spot in the play-offs once again.

After a disastrous start to the season, Adrian Lam's side have found their groove, made waves and look in real good nick at present.

However, they have a tough end to the season in which they will know every win will matter.

The Leopards face Leeds Rhinos (A), Bradford Bulls (H), Huddersfield Giants (A), St Helens (H) and Wakefield Trinity (H).

No one can deny that is a difficult Final Charge, but if Leigh want to make it to the Grand Final for the first time, they need to show their steel now.

7) St Helens (24 points)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of St Helens against Hull FC in the Betfred Super League

St Helens have five matches to try and ensure they do not make some unwanted history.

Saints have never missed out on the play-offs. Most recently they lost 20-12 to Hull KR in the semi-finals in 2025 as the Robins went on to complete the treble.

After their most recent loss to Hull FC, it is fair to say St Helens look down and out.

However, they will now refocus and aim for five wins out of five to be in with a shout. If they win all five, they move to 34 points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player St Helens chairman Eamonn McManus announced his side will take on Hull FC in a Super League clash in Dublin on April 25

Not only that, they face some of the other play-off chasing teams so some matches basically become worth four points.

They will take on Wakefield Trinity (A), Castleford Tigers (H), Leeds Rhinos (H), Leigh Leopards (A) and Hull KR (H).

Four out of their five remaining matches are against teams in the top six - talk about having to take your moment.

Will they do the unthinkable? If they do somehow find some form, that final-round contest against Hull KR could be extra tasty...

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Badri chases four-timer at Windsor
Sports.content:
Windsor takes centre stage on Monday with a six-race Flat meeting live on Sky Sports Racing.

7.15 Windsor - Badri seeks four-timer in Sprint Series Final

Badri seeks a four-timer in the feature race at Windsor, the Fitzdares Sprint Series Final Handicap over six furlongs.

This horse has been a credit to connections, winning 15 times in 75 starts with his last three runs resulting in success, all at Pontefract. That has taken him from 89-rated up to 99 which is his best mark since March 2024.

Another Abbot returns to Windsor looking to follow up his course-and-distance success two weeks ago after previously running a creditable race in behind Amazing Journey, who went on to to win the International Handicap on King George Day at Ascot. That form reads very well and he could be hard to beat.

Sudden Flight is a model of consistency, finishing second in his last three starts which included in behind Another Abbot two weeks ago. He does find winning hard to come by, though, having not won since July last year, but is now better off at the weights with William Haggas' charge and looks sure to run his race.

6.15 Windsor - Harry Knows and Keep Kicking On feature

Previous-winners Harry Knows and Keep Kicking On lock horns in the Fitzdares Nursery Handicap.

Harry Knows won in stylish fashion last time out at Windsor and received a three-pound rise for the success which might not be enough to stop him from continuing the winning sequence.

Keep Kicking On also arrives off the back of his first success over this track and trip when hitting the line readily three weeks ago and there could be more to come.

This Moment represents the connections of Bow Echo, dropping into a nursery for the first time and must be respected off 79 given the form of George Boughey and Billy Loughnane this season. He is interesting first time out after a gelding operation too.

5.45 Windsor - Mythological Star bids to defy penalty

Sports.title: Brennan secures FedEx Cup Playoffs spot with Wyndham Championship win
Sports.content:
Michael Brennan secured his place in the FedExCup Playoffs as he won the Wyndham Championship by three strokes from Beau Hossler.

Brennan had a run of five straight birdies between the fourth and eighth holes, and recovered from a bogey on the 11th by picking up further shots on the 13th and 18th holes, saving par on the 17th with an excellent second shot after running into the rough with his tee-shot.

Hossler, who shared the overnight lead with Brennan, had kept himself in touch with a birdie on the third and an eagle at the par-five fifth, but then bogeyed the ninth and 12th holes as Brennan surged forward.

"I did great for nine holes," Brennan said. "I felt really good on the front nine. Just playing my game, I was really staying within myself, hitting good shots.

Image: Brennan shot a final-round 64 at Sedgefield Country Club

"Felt like I was really in control. Got a little nervous around 10 and 11. I made a really nice par putt on 12 and that kind of steadied me a little bit going through and I'm just glad to make a few putts coming in.

"It's everything. I mean, I don't want to be done playing golf. I feel like I've played the best golf I have all year the last couple weeks.

"Unfortunately, a couple tough Sundays, but outside of that, I've been playing really solidly. This is my sixth week in a row and so seven's a lot, but I think I'm going to be perfectly happy running on fumes next week."

England's Harry Hall finished with a round of 65 to take a share of fifth place, one shot clear of compatriot Matt Wallace who had a share of seventh after he also closed with a 65.

Sports.title: UEFA signs joint letter slamming 'deception' as Infantino fallout continues
Sports.content:
UEFA, CONMEBOL and AFC have hit out at "deception" and a "fundamental breach of trust" around Gianni Infantino's botched World Cup stake sale plans to further raise the pressure on the under-fire FIFA president.

The three continental associations each signed a new open letter to the "football family" on Monday, without naming Infantino specifically but referring to a leader who "abandoned their duty" by breaking trust "through deception".

In the three-page document they again criticised the president's World Cup sale plans and rejected FIFA's claim that they had been a "mistake", adding: "There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the FIFA World Cup was a profound failure of judgment - not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions FIFA exists to serve."

UEFA, CONMEBOL and AFC had been the three confederations to reject Infantino's plan before its scrapping, while UEFA went further and announced a boycott of FIFA competitions - and last week confirmed the threat remained while Infantino is still in post.

The associations also hit out at the manner of a FIFA management committee meeting held in Morocco last Wednesday - a meeting which which ended with a statement publicly backing Infantino - for not instead addressing FIFA's wider senior leadership at its base in Switzerland.

"It is not the conduct of a custodian of the game, but of one who believes the game is answerable to him," the letter read. "There is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness."

The letter came around 24 hours after FIFA itself had hit out at "a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine" the governing body and president Infantino over claims surrounding his conduct at UEFA.

UEFA confirmed on Saturday a "departure payment" was made to a female employee alleged to have been in a relationship with Infantino when he was the European organisation's general secretary.

The Daily Telegraph reported the woman received a six-figure sum and UEFA confirmed a payment was made along with covering the fees for an MBA course, adding it was "in line" with regulations at the time.

The allegations intensified the position of Infantino, who worked at UEFA for 16 years and was its general secretary between 2009 and 2016 before being elected FIFA president, following his aborted plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

While not directly referencing UEFA's statement, FIFA accused Infantino's critics of trying to weaken his authority and have him removed from his role without a due re-election process.

Image: FIFA defended Infantino in a lengthy statement

A statement said: "It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its president.

"Those who do not have the support of FIFA's member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA's established democratic processes.

"Recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning FIFA and its president. Speculation and insinuation should not be presented as fact, and repetition does not make an allegation true.

"The FIFA president has dedicated more than 30 years of his professional life to European and world football, contributing to significant change in the game and, in particular, to broadening access, resources and opportunity across world football

"Change inevitably challenges established interests, but disagreement with that change cannot justify efforts to undermine the democratic mandate of FIFA's president or the institution he was elected to lead.

"FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to distort facts, amplify unsubstantiated allegations or manufacture distractions designed to undermine progress. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading, FIFA will challenge it directly and vigorously.

"FIFA's responsibility is to its 211 member associations and to football around the world. We will not be distracted or diverted from strengthening the organisation, delivering for our member associations and continuing the work of making football truly global. Through the FIFA president and the FIFA administration, our focus remains firmly on that mission, and we are more determined than ever to fulfil it."

Image: Infantino worked at UEFA for 16 years

Following the Daily Telegraph claims on Friday, a FIFA spokesperson was reported to have told the newspaper Infantino "strongly denies these categorically untrue allegations".

A UEFA spokesperson said: "We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for a MBA course at a local business school.

"The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time.

"Such regulations have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations - which apply to all UEFA employees at whatever level - reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation."

Sports.title: Golfer shoots 59 in final round en route to win on Korn Ferry Tour
Sports.content:
Frankie Harris made an 18-foot birdie putt on the final hole as he shot a 12-under 59 before winning the Korn Ferry Tour's Pinnacle Bank Championship in a play-off.

Harris shot an eight-under 27 on the back nine at The Club at Indian Creek with six birdies, an eagle and two pars added to four birdies and five pars across his front nine in Nebraska.

The 23-year-old, who beat Alistair Docherty in the play-off after both players ended at 22 under following the regulation 72 holes, is the ninth golfer worldwide to shoot a sub-60 final round and win the tournament.

Harris joins players including Bryson DeChambeau, who won LIV Golf Greenbrier in 2023 after ending with a 58, and Jim Furyk, who recorded a 58 in round four of the 2016 Travelers Championship.

Image: Harris beat Alistair Docherty in a play-off after shooting 59 in his final round in Omaha

'Shooting a 59 never crossed my mind'

Harris said afterwards: "The thought of a 59 never even crossed my mind. Honestly, like 100 per cent. I did not know I shot a 59 when I made that putt on 18.

"I knew I was playing well, but I was just trying to keep the pedal on the gas and finish strong.

"I was ready to crack my first beer once I finished the round, but then my caddie and I made a smart choice not do that because Alistair came in real hot.

"I knew it was going to come down to a play-off, so figured it was my time."

The victory moves Harris to No 29 on the Korn Ferry Tour points list, with the top 20 at the end of the campaign earning PGA Tour cards for 2027.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 1: Arsenal
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 1st (NB: this is not necessarily Ed Aarons’ prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 1st

Prospects

Even losing on penalties in the Champions League final could not take any of the gloss off last season as Arsenal ended their 22-year wait to be crowned Premier League champions. The celebrations have continued all summer after some wild scenes on the streets of north London on their return from Budapest, although concerns over the fitness of some key players after their exploits at the World Cup are mounting.

Arsenal have acted quickly to reinforce their midfield by signing Bruno Guimarães from Newcastle given Declan Rice’s workload must be managed very carefully after playing through neural pain in his hamstring and lower back since December. The arrival of Greece forward Christos Tzolis to replace Leandro Trossard also looks like a smart piece of business on the left-hand side of the attack. But with Vinícius Junior staying at Real Madrid, despite Arsenal’s best efforts, supporters will be hoping there is still a chance that the sporting director, Andrea Berta, could conjure up a heavyweight attacking signing before the window closes given Bukayo Saka’s fitness problems in recent seasons.

The back injury that will sideline William Saliba for an unknown period could prove even more central to Arsenal’s hopes of retaining their title. A defence that conceded 27 goals last year in the Premier League may struggle without the immense talents of the France defender, even if they can bring in Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa as hoped. Whether Arsenal can maintain their dominance from set pieces over the past two campaigns will also be crucial, with more scrutiny expected from video assistant referees after the fallout from their controversial victory at West Ham in May.

Not since 1935, when Arsenal became the second team to win three successive league titles, have they retained their crown. Having strengthened the deepest squad in the division still further, they will take some stopping again.

Off-field picture

Money definitely isn’t an issue for Stan Kroenke. Arsenal’s co-owner became America’s largest private landowner this year and has spent more than £1.5bn on new players since becoming the majority shareholder in 2011 through his holding company, Kroenke Sports & Entertainment (KSE). Next on the agenda is an upgrade to the Emirates Stadium that could increase the capacity of their home to more than 70,000. Talks have begun with the stadium’s original architects, Populous, over a project that could cost up to £500m. The much-criticised shirtsleeve deal with Visit Rwanda ended last season and has been replaced by the HR company Deel, itself controversial in some sections of the Arsenal fanbase, while Emirates have renewed their longstanding partnership until 2033.

Owner-fan relationship

Kroenke and his son Josh – who are co-chairs – clearly revelled in carrying out the Premier League trophy at Selhurst Park before it was presented to the captain, Martin Ødegaard, after Arsenal’s final game of the season in May. Having once been criticised for running the club “like an investment vehicle”, now they are praised for the enormous effect they have made. Kroenke Jr’s promise there would be “no standing still once this season ends” was an ominous sign to their rivals given KSE have a reputation as serial winners in a number of sports in America.

The manager

Mikel Arteta’s expected bumper new contract extension – that will make him one of the best-paid managers in the world – has yet to be confirmed, but there is no doubting his commitment to the cause. The Spaniard could not bear to watch as Manchester City’s challenge collapsed against Bournemouth last season and was in his back garden “building a fire” when Arsenal were confirmed as champions. With Pep Guardiola gone, Arteta has the opportunity to build a new winning dynasty of his own.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen The Gunners fans will be hoping to see Bruno Guimarães’ goal celebration on numerous occasions this season. Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

The arrival of Guimarães was another big statement of intent from Arsenal. The former Newcastle captain wants to win more trophies after capturing hearts and minds on Tyneside and he will provide several options in the already well-stacked engine room. As well as relieving the load on Rice, the versatile 28-year-old Brazil midfielder is capable of fulfilling a number of roles, from deep-lying playmaker to box-to box destroyer. While it remains to be seen how Arteta chooses to use Guimarães when he also has Martín Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ødegaard and Mikel Merino at his disposal, his talents will only add to the quality in Arsenal’s squad.

Stat attack

Referees have been told to pay much more attention to grappling during set-pieces this season so it will be interesting to see if this has any effect on Arsenal. Only three teams in the Premier League had a better non-penalty expected goal difference than the Gunners had from set plays alone.

Set for a breakthrough

Max Dowman was a record-breaking revelation as he dipped his toes into senior football for the first time last season and the signs are that the 16-year-old could be handed more opportunities after impressing again during pre-season. A brilliant goal and an assist against Girona capped a man-of-the-match display from the right flank. With Saka and Noni Madueke to be eased back in after returning from World Cup duty, Dowman is ready to add to his solitary Premier League start, against Crystal Palace on the final day of last season, and should appear more regularly in cup competitions.

World Cup impact

Rice and Saka arrived in the United States feeling the effects of a marathon season and it was to their immense credit that they played through the pain barrier and made it to England’s eighth match of the tournament. Only Thomas Tuchel knows why he left Saka on the bench in the semi-final against Argentina and his hat-trick in the third-place playoff a few days later showed how potent he can be even with an achilles problem. Both require an extended break before returning to the rigours of club football and Arsenal will give them as long as possible. But such is their importance that it will be sooner rather than later.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Endrick set for Villa loan? De Jong offered in Rodri deal?
Sports.content:
A sense of excitement is what Aston Villa need at the moment after selling off key players. What better way to create it than signing a prodigious talent from Real Madrid? The Villans have inquired about the Brazilian Endrick, who impressed on loan at Lyon last season, and may make a similar temporary move to the Premier League.

Manchester City are not particularly keen to sell Rodri but, with a year left on his contract money may well talk, especially if the midfielder wants to leave. Barcelona’s first bid was rejected but they are readying another. One idea is to offer Frenkie de Jong as part of the deal, so at least Enzo Maresca would have a shiny new midfielder to play with.

One player who could be leaving Camp Nou is the World Cup-winning goalscorer Ferran Torres, who has reportedly told Paris Saint-Germain he wants to pop across to the French capital. Not that a deal between the clubs has been agreed.

Another potential swap deal is on the cards between Everton and Crystal Palace. Calls have been made to discuss Dwight McNeil moving to Selhurst Park and Brennan Johnson swapping places with him at Hill Dickinson Stadium. The two wingers have struggled for game time perhaps a swap would reignite their careers. McNeil almost ended up at Selhurst Park in January before a late breakdown in talks left the player and his family furious.

Promoted Ipswich have been active in the market and could add the Bayer Leverkusen midfielder Exequiel Palacios. A bid has been faxed over, leaving the Tractor Boys to play the waiting game, but they may face competition for his signature.

After what must have been a lot of wrangling, Chelsea have agreed to loan Filip Jörgensen to sister club Strasbourg. The Blues are well-stocked with players and need to bin a few who can’t be sent to Strasbourg, so they may allow Jamie Gittens to head on loan to Roma.

The departure of Bruno Guimarães will prompt a rethink at Newcastle, who rather desperately need a new central midfielder. Sandro Tonali was sold a while back, giving the club some cash to play with, but they still seem to be thinking about signing João Palhinha who is not wanted at Bayern Munich The former Tottenham man Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is another option. Palhinha is also of interest to Aston Villa, who have made contact with the Bundesliga champions.

Manchester United are planning for the future with a move for the Leicester teenager Louis Page. The 18-year-old came through the academy ranks with the Foxes, but is naturally more than happy to take the leap from League One.

Sports.title: José Mourinho reveals he signed contract to succeed Alex Ferguson at Manchester United in 2013
Sports.content:
José Mourinho has revealed he signed a contract to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson as Manchester United manager in 2013 only to tearfully renege on the deal and return to Chelsea.

The football world was rocked when the Scottish great announced he was retiring having overseen a 13th Premier League title triumph during a spell of unrivalled dominance at Old Trafford.

United have failed to return to the top of the English game since Ferguson stepped down, with his successor, David Moyes, sacked after only 10 months in charge.

Mourinho was later brought in, spending two and a half years in charge from 2016, but revealed in a new Netflix documentary about his life that he had agreed to come earlier.

“I go to Chelsea in 2013 but in that period there is something nobody knows,” the Portuguese said in the documentary, which is entitled Mourinho. “I think I can say because I don’t hurt anyone with the truth, and I think the objective of this work that we are doing is to tell the truth. When I left Real Madrid, I signed with Manchester United to go to Manchester United after Sir Alex.”

Mourinho continued: “I was, of course, very flattered, because Manchester United has an incredible appeal. When I say Real Madrid is the biggest club in the world, I have to say that Manchester United is very, very close.

double quotation mark He phoned me and he was crying. He says: ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word to Chelsea.’ Sir Alex Ferguson

“But one thing is love for football, and another thing is love for a certain club. I think this is more powerful than love for football and, fundamentally, after Real Madrid, I needed to feel that I’m loved.”

Ferguson was one of the footballing figures interviewed for the new documentary and admits he was under the illusion Mourinho was accepting the offer, only for the situation to change in a matter of hours.

“Early evening he phoned me and he was crying,” the United great said. “And he says: ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word to Chelsea, and I’m not going to break my word.’ The reason he gave to me I could understand, but I was disappointed.”

Mourinho had a strong bond with Chelsea after leading them to two Premier League titles, an FA Cup and two League Cups during his first spell.

View image in fullscreen Alex Ferguson’s long spell as Manchester United manager ended in May 2013. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

The Portuguese parked differences with the Chelsea owner, Roman Abramovich, to return to Stamford Bridge after leaving Real Madrid, winning another league crown and League Cup before being sacked in December 2015.

“For me to lose the chance to be the coach to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson was dramatic, but I don’t regret because it was a decision that I made with my heart,” Mourinho, now back in charge of Real Madrid, said.

“And I think it is nature that says something that when you do something for love, you are never doing anything wrong. I think it’s nature. I did it for love.

“I went back with the feeling of, yes, I go home, but with big responsibility because what I did before is history, and you don’t want to destroy your legacy.”

Sports.title: La Liga president Javier Tebas says ‘Infantino era is over’ at Fifa
Sports.content:
Javier Tebas says Gianni Infantino’s position as Fifa president is untenable, claiming he is “destroying the very essence of football” while calling for reform at the highest levels of the game.

The La Liga president, who is a longstanding and vociferous critic of the current Fifa regime, said “the Infantino era is over” and called for control of the game to be expanded beyond the current “elite”.

While Tebas’s remarks will surprise no one within the game, they maintain the drumbeat of criticism directed against Infantino following his determination to continue in post despite his secret and subsequently quashed plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.

In an interview with French newspaper Le Monde, Tebas repeated his call for Infantino to resign, an appeal first made after the World Cup but before the sell-off scandal. “For me, Gianni Infantino’s time has long since passed,” he said.

“I’m not saying this because of recent events; I have noticed this style of management for a long time, though everyone else seems to be discovering it only now.

“Gianni Infantino is not someone who contributes to the growth of football. On the contrary, his projects are destroying the very essence of the sport: the national leagues.

“Football is not limited to the elite. For me, the Infantino era is over. What remains to be seen is when that will take effect and how the succession will unfold. I hope it is not just a matter of swapping out some people for others, but of a genuine overhaul.”

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino has received the backing of Fifa in spite of Uefa’s threat to boycott all its tournaments. Photograph: Sam Corum/PA

Infantino is battling to stay in post despite an increasingly coordinated attempt by European football officials and others to unseat the 56-year-old Swiss. Uefa has made it clear they regard Infantino’s continued leadership of world football as untenable, the Norwegian FA has called for the president to stand down and a number of European associations have withdrawn letters endorsing Infantino for another term at the head of Fifa.

Uefa confirmed on Saturday that a “departure payment” had been made to a female employee who is alleged to have been in a relationship with Infantino while he was the organisation’s general secretary more than a decade ago.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Daily Telegraph reported on Friday night that the woman received a six-figure sum after the alleged relationship, allegations Fifa dismissed as “categorically untrue”.

On Saturday night, Fifa published a statement accusing Infantino’s critics of attempting to remove him from office before the presidential election next March. “Those who do not have the support of Fifa’s member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa’s established democratic processes,” the statement read.

Infantino has also garnered support from prominent nations outside Europe, including the World Cup co-host Mexico and the finalists Argentina. Uefa say a proposed boycott of all Fifa tournaments remains in prospect, with the women’s Under-20 World Cup due to start in Poland on 5 September.

Sports.title: Hibernian stun Rangers at Ibrox while O’Neill misses Høgh treble in Celtic win
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes suffered a damaging home debut as Rangers manager with a 2-1 Premiership defeat to Hibernian compounded by striker Youssef Chermiti being carried off the pitch on a stretcher.

David Gray’s side took the lead in the 12th minute with a Josh Campbell penalty after the video assistant referee (VAR) had flagged up that Vanja Dragojevic, making his first Rangers start after signing from Partizan Belgrade, had fouled Jason Kerr in the area.

There was more woe before the break when Chermiti, subject to a failed bid by Galatasaray for a reported club record fee of £22million, having to go off after picking up an injury.

Rangers pushed forward relentlessly and were rewarded in the 85th minute when the Hibs defender Miguel Chaiwa turned the ball past the goalkeeper Raphael Sallinger.

However, in the third minute of added time, the substitute Callum Wright guided a shot into the far corner for a stunning win.

With Celtic and St Mirren both on six points from two games, Rangers are five behind with McInnes looking for his first win after three matches in the Ibrox hot seat.

Kasper Høgh scored a hat-trick, his first goals for Celtic, as the Scottish champions made light of the absence of their manager Martin O’Neill with a 5-1 win at Kilmarnock. O’Neill missed the trip to Rugby Park after what the club had said earlier this week was a “small procedure” in hospital.

No details were given about O’Neill’s operation, which came after the veteran Northern Irish manager took charge of Celtic’s win against Dundee in their first game of the season. But the club’s assistant manager, Shaun Maloney, speaking before Sunday’s kick-off, said O’Neill was on the mend. “He is doing better again,” Maloney told Sky Sports. “He came to the team hotel and spoke to the players but he just needs an extra few days.”

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s Kasper Høgh scores the first of his three goals against Kilmarnock. Photograph: Robert Perry/PA

O’Neill’s mood would doubtless have been improved by the performance of his side, with Celtic 3-0 ahead before half-time thanks to Høgh. The Danish striker, who joined in July from Bodø/Glimt, needed less than a minute to score his first Celtic goal, heading in at the back post from a cross by Arne Engels.

Høgh doubled Celtic’s lead in the 33rd minute, with Camilo Durán seizing on Johnly Yfeko’s pass out of defence. He combined with Benjamin Nygren to work the ball to Høgh on the left edge of the box, with the forward finishing well.

Two minutes later, Høgh had his hat-trick. Nygren slipping the ball right for Durán, whose cross took the Kilmarnock goalkeeper Max Stryjek out of play, with Høgh nodding into an empty net.

Celtic extended their lead early in the second half after they were effectively gifted a fourth goal by Stryjek. His pass out of defence went straight to Nygren in front of goal and his shot into the top corner made it 4-0.

Michael Schjønning-Larsen pulled a goal back for Kilmarnock in the 56th minute after finishing a well-worked move. But Celtic went four goals ahead again when Luke McCowan, moments after coming on, volleyed in from close range 15 minutes from time after Kilmarnock made a mess of trying to clear the ball from a corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s assistant manager Shaun Maloney took charge with Martin O’Neill still recovering from a procedure in hospital. Photograph: Robert Perry/PA

Three Hearts summer signings were on target as Wouter Vrancken belatedly got his reign up and running with a 4-0 win over Dundee United. The Belgian had suffered four consecutive defeats – three in Europe – since replacing Derek McInnes in June, but his new-look team tore United apart in their first home league game of the season.

Tom Renaud, Calvin Miller and Josh McPake all marked their first league outings at Tynecastle with goals, while last season’s talisman Cláudio Braga broke his duck for the campaign.

Hearts made a fast start as Renaud, a few days after notching against Benfica, unleashed a ferocious strike beyond Jack Walton from just short of 30 yards after being teed up by Braga in the fourth minute.

View image in fullscreen Josh McPake turns away after scoring Hearts’ fourth goal against Dundee United. Photograph: Malcolm Mackenzie/Getty Images

The home side were gifted the chance to double their lead when VAR spotted Daniel Bennie wrestling Jamie McCart to the ground in the box. Miller stepped up to fire the penalty straight down the middle.

Hearts killed off any hopes of a United fightback in the 56th minute when Braga drilled in a low angled shot from 12 yards out after being set up by Sabah Kerjota. McPake then marked his first competitive start for Hearts with his first goal as he tucked a clinical low finish beyond Walton after playing a one-two with Braga on the left of the box.

In Sunday’s other 3pm kick-off, Motherwell drew 0-0 at home to Falkirk.

On Saturday, Dundee beat Aberdeen 2-0 thanks to goals from Joe Westley and Joe Bevan while St Mirren edged St Johnstone 1-0 courtesy of Killian Phillips’ penalty.

Sports.title: Iraola says Liverpool have work to do as familiar frailties in defence prove costly
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola told his Liverpool team they have work to do after ­squandering a 2-0 lead against Monaco to lose a second successive pre-season friendly.

The former Bournemouth coach last managed a game at Anfield almost exactly a year ago in the memorable opener to the 2025-26 Premier League season, a game the Cherries were unfortunate to lose 4-2. Now on his debut in the home dugout, Iraola saw his team produce a similarly open display and lose again. It became clear Liverpool’s longstanding defensive frailties are still to be eliminated.

Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz scored in the first half as the hosts exhibited some free-flowing ­football, but Monaco dominated a ­second half that became fragmented as Iraola and Monaco’s Filipe Luís made wholesale changes.

“As soon as we have made some changes they start to get tired, we cannot sustain that level, so we have work to do,” Iraola told LFCTV on Liverpool’s “frustrating” regression after a bright start. “They were much better in the second half, in the same way we were better in the first half.”

After Liverpool beat Wrexham and Sunderland during a pre-season tour to the US, a 4-2 defeat against Leeds brought back memories of the struggles of last season. This result will cause some concerns with transfer activity dragging.

Ronald Araújo is at least due to arrive on loan from Barcelona. Although that deal is not yet complete and Alexis Mac Allister is still to return from World Cup duty, Iraola’s team to face Monaco was strong, with Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, and Lewis Koumas, 20, the only fringe players to start if you exclude Kostas Tsimikas, back from a loan at Roma. Jérémy Jacquet and Curtis Jones were not considered because of fitness doubts, with Iraola at pains not to “rush” Jaquet, who signed from Rennes for £50m, into action after a chequered time with injury.

Iraola said: “Jérémy, we were in doubt whether to pick him today, he should be fine for the next one. Curtis [there is] something wrong with his hip, [it] didn’t make sense to risk [him].”

Wirtz was sharp, testing Lukas Hradecky with an early shot. Isak’s opener on 16 minutes was met with a hearty cheer from the home faithful, perhaps not surprising given it was just the fourth time the Anfield crowd have been able to celebrate an Isak goal, competitive or otherwise.

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola was disappointed after watching Liverpool slip to a second successive friendly defeat. Photograph: Lewis Storey/Danehouse/Getty Images

The strike came after Ryan ­Gravenberch and Dominik ­Szoboszlai’s slick midfield exchange, the former then finding the Swede, who rifled low into the corner. Koumas and Wirtz both squandered presentable chances, but it was soon 2-0 when the German forced home after a ­goalmouth scramble.

Iraola cut a relaxed figure on the touchline throughout and was content with his side’s attacking fluidity. The Spaniard’s preference for a high defensive line was evident throughout, though Alisson was tested far less often than Hradecky until he had to face a 44th-minute penalty after Virgil van Dijk’s trip on Aleksandr Golovin. The Russian stroked home the spot-kick himself to make it 2-1 at the break, giving ­Alisson no chance.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wataru Endo for Ndukwe and Giorgi Mamardashvili for Alisson were the only half-time substitutions from Iraola, who made more sweeping changes just before the hour, with Rio Ngumoha, Milos Kerkez and the summer signing Víctor Muñoz among those introduced.

By that stage it was 2-2, after Mamardashvili had saved from Mika Biereth only to see the striker tap in the rebound. Monaco’s goals were greeted with eerie silence given there were almost no away fans. There were some groans from home supporters frustrated at seeing their side fritter away a two-goal lead but Ngumoha’s name was sung when he came on.

That Ngumoha was selected on the right wing – Mohamed Salah’s old stomping ground – was lost on nobody, nor was the fact that both the youngster and Muñoz were brought on rather than Federico Chiesa. The Italian did appear after 74 minutes along with Harvey Elliott, who was welcomed warmly back to Anfield after his nightmare on loan at Aston Villa.

Monaco carved out the better chances in the search for the next goal, with Flávio Nazinho firing wide, and Oumar Konaté failing to seize on a good through ball, before their 88th-minute winner stemmed from a corner swung in from the left, which Paris Brunner met with a sweet header.

There was no Anfield roar to push the hosts on to equalise as there would have been in a competitive match, and Liverpool’s side resembled a reserves squad by the end, but it was still a tame finish nonetheless. Only a double-header against Como – the first of which will be played behind closed doors – now remains before Iraola’s competitive debut away at Newcastle on 23 August, with his home league debut coming against Nottingham Forest a week later. The manager will demand an improvement in the next fortnight.

Sports.title: Seesaw draw in Malaysia gives Xabi Alonso food for thought at Chelsea
Sports.content:
Chelsea’s problems mounted as their pre-season tour came to an end in a strangely fiery draw against the Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim. The omens do not look promising with a bloated choice of forwards, echoes of their inexperience and indiscipline last season, and fewer than two weeks for the new manager, Xabi Alonso, to reintegrate key players and work with the entirety of his squad before they kick off the Premier League season against Fulham – managed by his old friend Álvaro Arbeloa – on 24 August.

Alonso, tasked with transforming a club that finished 10th in the Premier League last season into Champions League qualifiers, made 11 changes for the friendly against JDT. He rested players after beating Milan with a strong lineup only 24 hours earlier, 600 miles away.

While the defence and midfield were packed with teenagers, the front three – Estêvão Willian, Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson – would be welcomed by most Premier League clubs, having cost Chelsea more than £100m combined in the past three years.

Delap scored twice from the penalty spot – as many goals in 20 minutes as he managed in the entirety of his first season at Chelsea after joining from Ipswich last summer. The 23-year-old is believed to want to stay and fight for his place, having already proved his Premier League pedigree with 12 top-flight goals for Ipswich. Yet Alonso has so many options: João Pedro, one of the standout strikers last season; the new signing Danny Welbeck; and Jackson, who gave the club something to think about on his loan at Bayern Munich last season.

Emmanuel Emegha arrived recently from sister club Strasbourg, and may well go out on loan. They also still have Marc Guiu on the books.

Mykhailo Mudryk returning unexpectedly early from a drugs ban at the end of July was a curveball, adding to a rich choice of options on the wing including Cole Palmer, Estêvão – looking sharp again on Sunday after an injury that derailed the teenager’s promising first season at Stamford Bridge – and the record signing Morgan Rogers, who frequently played off the left for Aston Villa.

Plenty of time remains before the transfer window closes at the end of the month, but Chelsea’s squad stands at a staggering 41 players, with no European football next season and busy weeks of potential disruption ahead that will not ease Alonso’s stresses.

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap scores Chelsea’s second penalty of the evening. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

The JDT manager, Xisco Muñoz, was known for his fierce passion and aggressive football at Watford, and his players treated the game against Chelsea like a competitive fixture at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium in Johor. They flew into challenges, unsettling Chelsea’s players, competing with an intensity rarely seen in a preseason friendly. The visitors failed to keep tempers in check.

There were several flashpoints throughout the match. Delap and Jackson were needlessly booked for dissent, arguing with the referee about challenges on teammates. Estêvão was lucky not to be sent off after kicking out when he felt he was denied a penalty – instead shown a yellow card.

Geovany Quenda came off the bench and was also booked for launching into an entirely unnecessary challenge, as though settling a score. Sixteen-year-old Reggie Watson was booked in stoppage time, making it five yellow cards.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea received 11 red cards last season – twice as many as any other side and a club record – and Alonso has diverged from the owners’ policy of signing young by adding Welbeck, 35, and Jordan Henderson, 36. The club have not fielded a player over 30 since Thiago Silva, then 39, left in May 2024, but it might take more than a couple of veterans to sort the problem out.

JDT took the lead when they caught Chelsea on a break and Arif Aiman – known in these parts as the ‘Asian Messi’ – scored from a rapid move. Delap levelled just before half-time, then gave Chelsea the lead just after the hour. But JDT equalised three minutes later from Óscar Arribas’s heavily deflected free kick, then retook the lead when Bérgson finished into the bottom corner from distance with four minutes remaining. Mudryk, on in the 87th minute, produced the awkward cross that forced Antonio Glauder’s own goal with a minute on the clock, to avoid an embarrassing defeat.

Chelsea return to London after a punishing schedule. Their last three games were in three countries over five days: Juventus in Hong Kong, Milan in Indonesia and JDT in Malaysia – the last two in successive days, their plane landing in Malaysia at 3am on the day of the game.

Alonso has only two weeks – and one final friendly against Real Sociedad on Saturday – to work with the £117m signing Rogers, the injury-prone captain Reece James and the disgruntled star Enzo Fernández, all due back at the club’s Cobham training ground this week following extended World Cup breaks. Then the season will kick off – and the fun and games will really begin.

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Digne returns to PSG from Villa, Fulham agree £30m deal for Charles
Sports.content:
France defender Lucas Digne has completed his return to Paris Saint-Germain from Aston Villa on a three-year contract.

The 33-year-old full-back, who featured in six of Les Bleus’ World Cup matches this summer, had two years left on his contract with the Midlands club, with PSG triggering a reported release clause of between £6m-£7m.

Villa confirmed Digne’s exit on their website, adding that he is “a consummate professional, who was highly regarded by his fellow players and staff alike”.

He made 182 appearances in all competitions for Villa, scoring four goals and making 24 assists, after joining from Everton in a £25m deal in January 2022. He played a key role for Unai Emery’s side as they won the Europa League last season.

The Frenchman made 30 Ligue 1 appearances in a three-year spell at PSG until 2016, when he moved on to Barcelona. He told PSG’s website: “I am very honoured to be returning to Paris Saint-Germain following the wonderful experience I had here more than 10 years ago.”

Fulham have sought to bolster their midfield by spending £30m on Southampton’s Shea Charles.

Charles, a Northern Ireland international and breakout star of the last Championship season, is expected to sign a five-year deal at Craven Cottage once a medical assessment and legal formalities are completed.

View image in fullscreen Shea Charles was a breakout star in the Championship last season, helping Southampton to reach the playoffs. Photograph: Matt Watson/Southampton FC/Getty Images

Fulham will pay an initial fee of £26m, with another £4m dependent on performance, with the size of the fee believed to have ultimately deterred alternative interest from Leeds.

The 22-year-old played 2,000 minutes in the Championship last season as Southampton reached the playoffs before being excluded following revelations of spying against opponents. At Fulham, Charles will be expected to act as the linchpin of the midfield following the sale of Sasa Lukic to Ipswich earlier in the weekend.

Charles joins the young forwards Jonah Kusi-Asare and Gonzalo García as well as 21-year-old attacking midfielder César Palacios on the list of summer signings as Fulham seek to reduce the average age of their squad following the switch of manager from Marco Silva to the former Real Madrid B team coach Álvaro Arbeloa.

Trevoh Chalobah’s move to Como from Chelsea has been confirmed, in a deal worth an initial £25.7m. Terms for a five-year contract were agreed last week, but as the move was announced on Sunday, the England defender said he was “thrilled and honoured” to be joining Cesc Fàbregas’s side.

The pair overlapped at Stamford Bridge towards the end of the Spaniard’s time playing in England, and Chalobah said: “It’s an ambitious, rising project, and working with Cesc Fàbregas again is truly special. I can’t wait to bring my experience to the team, feel the incredible atmosphere at the stadium, and connect with the fans.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Fàbregas said: “Trevoh is a leader who can raise the level of the team, and I am very happy that he has chosen Como.”

Gustavo Hamer has completed a move from the Championship, this time renewing his relationship with Coventry after leaving Sheffield United for a fee of £6m plus add-ons. The Brazilian-born talent will become the Sky Blues’ sixth signing since returning to the top flight, with two big-ticket deals, £24m goalkeeper Carl Rushworth and £25m Ghanaian international midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi, joining in the last week alone.

View image in fullscreen Trevoh Chalobah will be linking up Cesc Fàbregas after joining Como on a five-year deal Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

Hamer was a key part of Mark Robins’s Coventry side as they reached the FA Cup semi-final and Championship playoff final two years ago, only for the attacking midfielder to then leave the club in a £15m deal with the promoted Blades. Following immediate relegation and a misfiring season last term, Hamer will begin a second stint at the CBS Arena, this time under Frank Lampard.

Midfielder Idrissa Gueye has joined Saudi Pro League newcomers Diriyah. The 36-year-old left Everton at the end of last season and arrives at his new club as a free agent. Gueye played in all four of Senegal’s matches at this summer’s World Cup as his country progressed to the last 32.

Elsewhere, Hull completed the signing of the Swedish wing-back Elliot Stroud from Mjallby. The 24-year-old featured in every game for his country at the World Cup and has signed a four-year deal. Reports also continue to link Sporting’s centre-half Ousmane Diomande with a £30m move to Nottingham Forest, with the Ivorian international said to be travelling to the UK from Portugal on Sunday in order to complete his medical. Diomande is understood to be the new Forest manager Oliver Glasner’s first-choice signing, and a player seen as having a key role to play in the German’s preferred 3-4-3 setup.

Sports.title: What time is 2026 UEFA Super Cup? World Cup banned referee to oversee PSG vs Aston Villa
Sports.content:
What time is 2026 UEFA Super Cup? World Cup banned referee to oversee PSG vs Aston Villa

One of the opening games of the 2026/27 campaign is a clash between the two leading European champions this week.

Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain take on Europa League victors Aston Villa in the UEFA Super Cup on Wednesday night.

3 PSG won their second consecutive Champions League, returning to the Super Cup Credit: Getty

PSG defeated Arsenal in the final of UEFA's elite competition, claiming the title for the second straight year by sinking the Gunners.

The French giants beat the Premier League champions on penalties following a 1-1 draw, as Gabriel sent his decisive spot-kick over.

They are also the reigning Super Cup winners after beating Tottenham in the game last term, so they are aiming to go back-to-back in this clash.

As for Aston Villa, they won the Europa League with a comfortable 3-0 win over German side Freiburg in Istanbul.

This will be Villa's first Super Cup appearance since 1983, having historically won their first European title in 44 years.

Somali referee Omar Artan was appointed as the lead official for the match after he was denied entry to the United States to officiate at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

When is the 2026 UEFA Super Cup?

The 2026 UEFA Super Cup will be played this Wednesday - August 12.

Kick-off is set for 8pm UK time, which is 9pm local time.

It will be held at the Red Bull Arena in Salzburg, Austria.

This is the first time a UEFA final has been played at this stadium, which is the home of Austrian giants Red Bull Salzburg.

3 Aston Villa are going to take on PSG after winning the Europa League last season Credit: Getty

The venue staged multiple games at EURO 2008 and will become the 14th ground to host the match since the competition switched from being hosted every year in Monaco 13 years ago.

Sports.title: Why is Community Shield not at Wembley this weekend? Arsenal face Man City as season opener moved out of England
Sports.content:
Why is Community Shield not at Wembley this weekend? Arsenal face Man City as season opener moved out of England

The Community Shield is a staple of pre-season in England - but it will not be staged in the country for the first time in two decades.

Fans across the world will tune in as Premier League champions Arsenal take on FA Cup winners Manchester City.

3 Arsenal could be the team to beat again this season as they look to defend their crown in the Premier League Credit: Getty Images - Getty

The Gunners head into the match aiming to build on their title-winning campaign, following a long-awaited success last term.

Meanwhile, Enzo Maresca will manage his first game as Man City manager and kick off the post-Pep Guardiola era.

Why is the Community Shield not at Wembley Stadium this year?

A major change of venue will see the clash move away from Wembley Stadium to an iconic ground that last hosted the event in 2006.

This is due to scheduling issues with pre-planned summer concerts taking place at the traditional venue.

The Weeknd is booked at England's national football stadium, performing his 'After Hours Til Dawn Stadium Tour with Playboi Carti'.

The official statement released by the FA confirmed supporters will have to cross the border into Wales for the clash.

They stated: "The 2026 FA Community Shield will be played at Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Sunday 16 August."

The event is historically held on the weekend before the Premier League commences, with this season on August 22.

This meant organisers had to target mid-August, which unfortunately clashed with the concert dates.

The Principality Stadium in Cardiff, a 74,500-capacity venue, offers a strictly neutral ground for both competing clubs, ensuring that fans of both teams face a journey.

3 Palace won the Community Shield at Wembley last year Credit: Getty

The Welsh national ground has hosted the Community Shield on six occasions between 2001 and 2006.

During that period, Arsenal played in four of the meetings, and won two.

Over the six years the fixture was relocated, only four teams competed across the border: Liverpool, Manchester United, Arsenal, and Chelsea.

In 2022, the fixture was also moved to the King Power Stadium due to Wembley Stadium hosting the Women's Euro 2022 final.

And in 2012, the game was also moved to Villa Park to host Man City and Chelsea as Wembley hosted the final of the 2012 Olympic football tournament.

The Manchester outfit were victorious on the day, winning 3-2.

3 Maresca's first competitive match in charge will be in Cardiff Credit: Getty

When is the Community Shield?

The 2026 FA Community Shield will take place this Sunday - August 16.

Kick-off for the match is scheduled for 3pm and will be held at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

Who won the 2025 Community Shield?

Crystal Palace won last year's edition against Liverpool after securing their first-ever FA Cup.

The Eagles beat the Reds 3-2 on penalties at Wembley after playing out a 2-2 draw in normal time.

Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr scored for Palace in the draw, with Hugo Ekitike and Jeremie Frimpong netting for Liverpool.

Marc Guehi lifted the trophy as captain under Oliver Glasner, but he will be representing Man City on this year's occasion.

Similarly, Eberechi Eze also featured in a Palace shirt at Wembley last summer, but will be lining up for Arsenal instead.

Sports.title: What time is Carabao Cup second round draw? Chelsea and Tottenham enter with draw split into sections
Sports.content:
What time is Carabao Cup second round draw? Chelsea and Tottenham enter with draw split into sections

The Carabao Cup has kicked off the new English football season and the second round draw is coming up fast.

An action-packed summer weekend of cup football has seen teams progress or crash out early and the focus will now shift to the next round's draw.

3 The journey to lifting the Carabao Cup trophy is officially underway Credit: Getty

For successful clubs in Round One, they could well be handed a huge tie in the second round, as some Premier League giants join.

Both Chelsea and Tottenham are going to be in the Round Two draw, having not qualified for Europe last season.

There are also another nine Premier League sides getting involved, potentially being put at risk of a major upset.

Here's all you need to know about the Carabao Cup draw...

When is the Carabao Cup second round draw?

The draw for Round Two of the Carabao Cup will take place on Monday, August 10.

The ball picking will commence at approximately 7:20pm.

It will be held before Plymouth Argyle face local rivals Exeter City in what is the final game of the first round.

Second round ties will be played on the week commencing August 24.

3 Xabi Alonso is set to find out his first Carabao Cup opponent as Chelsea boss Credit: Getty

How to follow the Carabao Cup draw

The second round draw will be broadcast live on Sky Sports Football in the build-up to the Devon derby.

It will be part of their match coverage from Home Park.

talkSPORT and talkSPORT.com will also be right across the latest.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

3 Tottenham are entering the competition at the second round after a poor last season Credit: AFP

Which Premier League clubs are joining?

There are 11 Premier League clubs joining the Carabao Cup at the second round, with nine others not yet involved.

Chelsea and Spurs are among the 11 sides without European football, with Newcastle and Nottingham Forest in the same boat.

Leeds also won't be playing in Europe, along with Everton, Brentford, Fulham, and newly-promoted Coventry, Ipswich and Hull.

Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool and Manchester United are four of the nine clubs joining the Carabao Cup in the third round.

How does the second round draw work?

The Carabao Cup second round follows the same format as the first round, splitting the competition into regions.

Teams are split into Northern and Southern sections.

So, they will be drawn against a club that are in their region.

This will then change for the third round, when all teams can be drawn against each other no matter their location.

Ball numbers for the draw will be confirmed shortly before it begins.

Sports.title: Arsenal told to make Gabriel Martinelli U-turn and reject £145m-rated replacement
Sports.content:
Andy Townsend would not swap Gabriel Martinelli with Bradley Barcola, claiming the latter is not worth his astronomical price tag.

Barcola's future at Paris Saint-Germain remains uncertain this summer and has already been the subject of interest from Liverpool.



3 Barcola faces plenty of competition for a starting berth at PSG Credit: Getty

However, Arsenal could be tempted to enter the Barcola sweepstakes after leading target Vinicius Junior opted to sign a bumper new contract to stay at Real Madrid.

Yet any move for Barcola will cost the Gunners a pretty penny, with the winger valued by PSG at approximately £145m.

Should a deal be completed for Barcola at that price, he would become the third-most expensive player in history, behind only Neymar and Kylian Mbappe.



But Townsend urged Arsenal to avoid forking out the eye-watering sum and keep Martinelli instead amid interest in the Brazilian from Galatasaray.

Barcola to Arsenal?

"I totally got going for Vini Jr but I don't get going for just another one," Townsend said on talkSPORT Breakfast.



"I don't see Barcola at the levels others do. I don't see him at anything like that sort of money.

"I think he is way behind (Kvicha) Kvaratskhelia and (Desire) Doue. Personally, I think they are far better players.



"I don't think he's got the end product in his game to warrant £140m-odd, no chance. I don't think I'd swap Martinelli for him.

"Honestly, I think Martinelli knows this division, has proven himself to be a valuable member of Arsenal's team.

"And I don't see it's that much of a massive trade-up for the sort of money that they'd need to invest in him."

3 Martinelli has made over 270 appearances for the Gunners since he joined in 2019 Credit: Getty



Martinelli could be on the chopping block at the Emirates given he is into the final year of his contract.

However, Arsenal have the option to extend the Brazilian's deal by a further 12 months.

Over the course of his career in north London, Martinelli has netted 62 goals in 278 appearances across all competitions.

Yet only one of those goals was scored in last season's Premier League along with just 11 starts, signifying Martinelli's reduced presence in his favoured left wing position.



Arsenal have already sold Leandro Trossard, who was another left wing option, to Besiktas, although he has since been replaced by Christos Tszolis.

Martinelli's Arsenal exit

Townsend admitted there would be some merit to letting Martinelli go given the need for Mikel Arteta to keep his squad fresh, but losing both the Brazilian and Trossard in the same window would be a blow.

3 Arteta is hoping to lead his squad to back-to-back Premier League titles Credit: Getty

"Honestly, I think it's not like they're wanting Martinelli to necessarily go, I don't think that's ever going to be the case," Townsend said.



"However, if they got proper money for him, they might be prepared to trade. Trading players for Mikel Arteta keeps everything alive and keeps everything a little fresher around the camp, which is very important for any club.

"But losing Trossard for the money they lost him for, I thought that was a slightly strange one in some ways because he was always good value for a really important goal, always a clever player coming off the bench and wanting to effect the game."

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho made shock U-turn on Manchester United job and broke down in tears to Alex Ferguson
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho made shock U-turn on Manchester United job and broke down in tears to Alex Ferguson

Jose Mourinho tearfully reneged on his decision to replace Alex Ferguson as Manchester United boss due to his love for Chelsea.

The Special One has revealed he signed a contract to take over the legendary Scotsman in 2013 when he stepped down after 27 years of service.



4 Mourinho was lined up to replace Ferguson at United - only for Chelsea to come calling Credit: AFP - Getty

At the time, Mourinho was in charge of Real Madrid, where he would later have his contract ripped up by mutual consent following the Copa del Rey final defeat to Atletico Madrid.

As for United, Ferguson announced his decision to retire on May 8, 2013, with Everton boss David Moyes named as his replacement a day later.

But in a new three-part Mourinho Netflix docuseries which is released on August 11, the iconic Portuguese boss declared he had first dibs.



Though he was left a blubbering mess when informing Ferguson of his decision to shun the chance when beloved club Chelsea came calling - six years after he was sacked at Stamford Bridge.

No way, Jose

Mourinho, who would eventually go on to manage United in 2016, said: "I go to Chelsea in 2013, but in that period there is something nobody knows.



"I think I can say because I don’t hurt anyone with the truth, and I think the objective of this work that we are doing is to tell the truth.

"When I left Real Madrid, I signed with Manchester United to go to Manchester United after Sir Alex.”



He added: "I was, of course, very flattered, because Manchester United has an incredible appeal.

"When I say Real Madrid is the biggest club in the world, I have to say that Manchester United is very, very close.

“But one thing is love for football, and another thing is love for a certain club.

4 Mourinho was Ferguson's top priority to replace him, with the Special One in tears after going back on his vow



"I think this is more powerful than love for football and, fundamentally, after Real Madrid, I needed to feel that I’m loved."

Are you Fer real?

Ferguson meanwhile recalled: "[Mourinho] was offered a job, yes. I sat him down and explained the situation.

"And as far as I was concerned, he was accepting. And then within hours, it changed.

"Early evening he phoned me and he was crying, and he says, ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word to Chelsea, and I’m not going to break my word.’



"The reason he gave to me I could understand, but I was disappointed.”

Mourinho, who won two Premier League titles, one FA Cup and two League Cups, would bring more silverware back to west London during his second spell.

4 Mourinho won a third Premier League title with Chelsea during his second spell in charge Credit: Getty

Another Premier League and League Cup medal was added to his trophy cabinet, before he was axed two-and-a-half-years later in December 2015.



And Mourinho has insisted he does not regret his decision to initially spurn United, as he stated: "For me to lose the chance to be the coach to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson was dramatic.

"But I don’t regret because it was a decision that I made with my heart.

“And I think it is nature that says something that when you do something for love, you are never doing anything wrong. I think it’s nature. I did it for love.

“I went back with the feeling of, yes, I go home, but with big responsibility because what I did before is history, and you don’t want to destroy your legacy."



Five months after his Chelsea exit, United were back in for Mourinho, where he this time jumped at the opportunity.

4 Mourinho guided United to Europa League glory in his opening season Credit: getty

In his first season at the Theatre of Dreams, he guided the club to Europa League, League Cup and Community Shield glory, before being axed in December 2018.

And this summer saw Mourinho return to another club in Real Madrid, with club president Florentino Perez whisking him in for a second crack 13 years after his initial departure.
