World.title: Uttarakhand Forward 2.0 | Prasanna Kumar Patro lays out Uttarakhand’s ecotourism roadmap
World.content:
Uttarakhand Forward 2.0 is the second edition of The Times of India's flagship video series spotlighting the state's journey of growth, innovation and transformative governance.

Through exclusive conversations with policymakers, administrators, industry leaders, educationists and experts, the series explores the ideas, initiatives and vision shaping Uttarakhand's future across infrastructure, clean energy, education, tourism, sustainability and more. The campaign highlights the policies driving progress, the challenges and opportunities ahead, and the roadmap for the state's next phase of development.

Can tourism and conservation go hand in hand?

As Uttarakhand balances growing tourism with the need to protect its rich forests and wildlife, the conversation around sustainable development has never been more important.

In this episode of Uttarakhand Forward 2.0, Richa Jain Kalra speaks with Prasanna Kumar Patro, MD, Ecotourism Development Corporation, CCF Ecotourism & CCF (HRD), Department of Forest, Government of Uttarakhand, about the state's vision for preserving its natural heritage while creating sustainable livelihoods.





The discussion explores ecotourism, forest conservation, human-wildlife conflict, climate change, forest fires, biodiversity, community participation through Van Panchayats, and the role of local communities in protecting Uttarakhand's ecosystems.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

From mass tourism to value tourism

Mr. Patro outlined an ecotourism vision centred on smaller destinations, local participation and low-impact travel. âExperiential tourism is very important,â he said, stressing the need to move from mass tourism towards value tourism.

What does the road ahead look like?

The conversation also explored livelihoods, Van Panchayats and the need to spread tourism to remote areas while reducing pressure on popular destinations. Looking ahead, Patro said Uttarakhand should develop smaller destinations that are âless capital intensive, less carbon footprintâ, while building on the stateâs natural strengths to emerge as a leading ecotourism destination.

World.title: 'Deep links with AAP': BJP calls CJP protest at Jantar Mantar Arvind Kejriwal's 'pet project'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Sunday turned its guns on the AAP over the CJP protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, alleging that the demonstration was a "pet project" of Arvind Kejriwal-led party. The saffron party also alleged that Kejriwal's party aimed at targeting Prime Minister

rather than addressing education reforms or the NEET paper leak.

BJP IT department head Amit Malviya made the allegation on X while targeting former Delhi chief minister

over remarks he allegedly made in a video circulating online.

Malviya shared the purported video in which Kejriwal can be heard saying in Hindi, "Is baar jitne log aaye the sadkon par, wo kis liye aaye the? Wo kewal mujhe nahin lagta ki Dharmendra Pradhan ka istifa mangne aaye rahe. Matlab agar main crude bhasha mein boloon, to Modi ji ko thokne aaye the.

(The people who took to the streets this time, what did they come for? I don't think they came merely to demand Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.

To use crude language, they came to take on Modi ji)."

However, the video's authenticity could not be verified.

Several BJP leaders, including former Delhi BJP chief Virendra Sachdeva, also condemned Kejriwal over his alleged remarks about Modi.

The BJP's Jammu and Kashmir unit said in a post on X, "Kejriwal has finally exposed his pet project -- the Cockroach Janta Party.





The agenda was never accountability or education reform. From day one, it was about one thing: targeting PM Modi."

BJP IT cell chief alleged that Kejriwal had effectively admitted that the Jantar Mantar protest, presented as a students' movement, was actually a sponsored political campaign against the prime minister.

"It was always evident that Cockroach Janta Party (

CJP

) founder Abhijeet Dipke and "his gang" had deep links with the AAP, Malviya said.

"But after the protest, the cockroaches went rogue, stopped taking Arvind's calls and forced the insecure Kejriwal to spill the beans on the true motive behind the protests," he claimed.

The BJP leader further accused the opposition parties of using students for political purposes.

"Your children were used as cannon fodder for the AAP and Congress's political agenda. Never forget that. They could have been hurt, embroiled in violence, or had their lives ruined.

But that didn't happen, thanks to the exemplary restraint shown by the law-enforcement agencies," Malviya added.

He also called for those who allegedly led the protest to be exposed, accusing them of abandoning it at the right moment to protect themselves and their alleged sponsors, naming Rahul Gandhi and Arvind Kejriwal.

BJP Rajya Sabha member Swati Maliwal also hit out at Kejriwal, alleging that students had been peacefully raising their concerns until he attempted to "hijack the movement and turn it into a political opportunity".

"Arvind Kejriwal says in an interview: 'Jo log sadak pe aaye the, wo Modi ji ko thokne aaye the.' What kind of a language is this? Does he even know what he's saying?" Maliwal said in a post on X, referring to the purported video.

"First he founded, funded and directed CJP, then hijacked the peaceful movement of students and tried to turn it violent as was done in Bangladesh and Nepal!... His dictatorial tendencies are out in the open, and it's clear that he can do anything to capture power.

Such people are a danger to democracy!" the BJP MP added.

Delhi minister Kapil Mishra also targeted Kejriwal, accusing him of using "Maoist-style language" while referring to the prime minister.

"This is not a symbol of any 'revolutionary uprising' on his part, but rather the final, desperate cry of his moral and linguistic bankruptcy," Mishra said on X.

World.title: 'Either guilty or incompetent': Rahul Gandhi seeks Amit Shah's statement on police action against protesters
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition

has stepped up his attack on the Centre, taking direct aim at Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister

over the police crackdown on students protesting at Delhi's Jantar Mantar over the NEET paper leak.

The students' prolonged agitation eventually led to one of their key demands being met, with Dharmendra Pradhan resigning as Union education minister.

However, Rahul Gandhi, while sharing his column published in a daily newspaper, continued to target the government over the alleged police action against protesters. Referring to the reported use of force, he questioned how the Modi government responds to young people demanding answers about their future.

He wrote in his post on X: "Pellet guns, Nail-studded lathis, tear gas fired at students who were peacefully asking questions about their own future. Young women beaten by policemen, many injured on their private parts. Minors with broken bones. This is how the Modi government answers a question."

Rae Bareli MP then turned his focus to Amit Shah, questioning his absence from Parliament and accusing him of remaining silent over the incident.





Rahul said, "And the home minister? Nearly 20 days and Amit Shah has not come to Parliament to answer for it. Every Opposition motion for a discussion has been rejected. His silence is not an oversight - it is approval of the violence. He is either culpable or incompetent."

He added, "We demand a Supreme Court monitored inquiry. And we will not stop fighting until he is held accountable."

In his column, Rahul recalled meeting students who were injured during the protests and questioned the Centre's handling of the incident. He argued that power in the government is highly "centralised" and pointed out that the

and Rapid Action Force (RAF), deployed at Jantar Mantar on July 20, report to Amit Shah-led Union home ministry.

He presented two possibilities: either Shah "authorised" the police action or he had "no idea that it was taking place".

"The Narendra Modi government prides itself on its centralised control. Whether it is a mission to Mars or an Olympic medal, it repeatedly trumpets that the credit is due to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah. Nothing moves without their approval."

"The violence happened in the heart of Delhi, barely 500 metres from Parliament.

Both the security forces deployed, the Delhi Police and the Rapid Action Force (RAF), report directly to the home minister," he added.

LoP in Lok Sabha said Shah's failure to address Parliament over the incident raises questions about his responsibility as Home Minister.

He said, "There are only two possibilities. First, he authorised the attack on the students - in which case he is culpable. Second, he had no idea that it was taking place - which means that he is entirely incompetent.

Either way, as Home Minister, what happened on that day is his responsibility, and he must resign."

"Instead, his inaction proves that he approves of the attack on students. He has not ordered any inquiry or even issued a statement. He has refused to come to Parliament, and motions filed," the column read.

The Congress and the INDIA bloc have repeatedly demanded a statement from Amit Shah in Parliament and have staged protests both inside and outside the House over the issue.

On Monday, another Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi also demanded statement from Amit Shah in Parliament.

Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju, however, has maintained that the Opposition cannot dictate which minister should come to Parliament and make a statement, saying the decision rests with the government.

World.title: Jharkhand students protest LIVE: Protestors reach State Assembly premises; police use tear gas, water cannons
World.content:
Thousands of job aspirants, protesting against irregularities in various recruitment examinations in Jharkhand, joined the march to the State assembly on Monday (August 10, 2026). Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on a hunger strike for nine days in protest against exam irregularities, also joined the march, despite losing 10.5 kg. He was seen carrying a portrait of former Jharkhand Chief Minister Shibu Soren.

Also read: For Jharkhand’s Adivasi youth, competitive exams are about finding a voice in the system that governs them

The Jharkhand government on Sunday (August 9, 2026) agreed to cancel the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) preliminary examination and the JPSC backlog examinations held in 2023 and 2025 following six hours of discussions with protesting student groups. However, the students remained firm on their demand for a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities in the JSSC-CGL examination and said the agitation would continue. The announcement came even as all three JPSC members resigned and Chief Minister Hemant Soren assured protesters that “justice will be delivered with full transparency”.

Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) and JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, said they want cancellation of JSSC-CGL and all exams connected to the TSR Data Processing Private Limited Agency, a blacklisted entity.

World.title: Jharkhand CID arrests ex-JPSC chairperson over alleged irregularities in recruitment exams
World.content:
Jharkhand CID on Monday (August 10, 2026) arrested former JPSC chairperson L. Khiangte in connection with alleged irregularities in the recruitment examinations, a top official of the state probe agency said.

Mr. Khiangte, who was appointed as Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) chairperson in February last year after he retired as the State’s chief secretary, tendered his resignation on July 22.

“We have arrested former JPSC chairperson L Khiangte in connection with irregularities in recruitment examinations,” Additional Director General (CID), Manoj Kaushik, told PTI.

Also read: Jharkhand student protest LIVE updates

Mr. Khiangte had been questioned four times since July 28.

The arrest comes a day after all three JPSC members resigned amid massive protests by aspirants over alleged irregularities in recruitment tests conducted by the agency.

With Mr. Khiangte’s arrest, the number of people arrested by CID in this case has risen to 20.

He had resigned as JPSC chairperson a day before the CID searched multiple locations, including his official residence, in connection with the alleged irregularities.

Mr. Khiangte, however, said he “voluntarily chose to resign” to ensure an impartial investigation into the matter.

World.title: Supreme Court allows Abhishek Banerjee to travel abroad for eye treatment
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Monday (August 10, 2026) permitted Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee to travel abroad for three weeks for eye treatment while noting that every individual has a right to travel abroad and choose the medical assistance he wants to receive.

A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant was hearing a petition filed by Mr. Banerjee against a Calcutta High Court order refusing a restriction imposed on him to travel abroad. The travel restriction was imposed on him in a case concerning an alleged provocative remark made during the 2026 State Assembly election campaign while staying his arrest.

Additional Solicitor General S.V. Raju, for the State of West Bengal, said Mr. Banerjee had 16 criminal cases arraigned against him, and there was a probability he may flee. The law officer said there were enough medical facilities for him in India and he need not go abroad.

“That is his choice. Every individual has a right to go abroad. Every individual has the right to choose the medical assistance he should get,” Justice Joymalya Bagchi, on the Bench, remarked.

Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, for Mr. Banerjee, submitted that his client had a diplomatic passport issued during the ‘Operation Sindoor’ outreach. The government could easily trace his movements from the passport, the senior counsel said in an effort to allay fears that the TMC MP would abscond.

Mr. Raju said the State wanted to test the veracity of his claims for medical attention, and the need to go abroad for treatment.

“We want to test what has been stated, whether he actually requires consultation or not,” Mr. Raju said.

Justice Bagchi responded, “Let him go. Let him get himself checked. In the meantime, you start another criminal case against him if you find the documents [medical records, etc.] are forged”.

“I think the State is weighed with much more investigative jobs. You have said this individual is alleged to be involved in grave allegations, but you have not taken any steps against him. Please do not make this situation worse,” Justice Bagchi addressed the State

The Court directed Mr. Banerjee to share details of his flight, itinerary, place of residence and hospital abroad.

World.title: Russia’s share in India’s oil imports jump to all-time high of 48% despite 100% tariffs threat from U.S.
World.content:
At a time when the U.S. looks all set to enact legislation to impose a tariff of up to 100% on India for its Russian oil imports, an analysis of the latest data shows Russia’s share in India’s oil imports rose to an all-time-high of 48% in June 2026.

Editorial | Oil conundrum: On India’s energy imports from Russia

The U.S. Senate last week passed the bipartisan Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 which seeks to levy tariffs of up to 100% on countries that continue to buy Russian oil and gas, and that were the largest purchasers of these products from Russia over the previous year. India qualifies for tariffs under these criteria.

The Bill still requires to be passed by the U.S. House of Representatives before it becomes law.

An analysis by The Hindu of the latest data from the Ministry of Commerce and Industry shows that India significantly lowered its total crude oil imports in June 2026. In terms of volume, June crude oil imports at 18.2 million metric tonnes (MMT) were down 16.5% compared to May 2026, and were 13% lower than in June last year.

However, elevated crude oil prices this year have meant that the oil import bill, while 22% lower in June 2026 than in May, was still 40% higher than in June of last year.

Russia’s share at historic high

While India drastically cut down on overall oil imports, its purchases from Russia bucked this trend. That is, India imported 8.7 MMT of Russian oil in June 2026, which was just 1% lower than in May, and 25% higher than in June of last year.

As a result of this strategy, Russia’s share in India’s crude oil imports jumped to 48% in terms of quantity and 48.6% in terms of the value. Russia’s share has been rising consistently every month since March and the outbreak of the war in West Asia.

According to the U.S. Bill, the tariffs would apply on a country that was among the five largest importers of crude oil or natural gas from Russia during the 12 months preceding the date of the enactment of the Act, and that then continues to import oil or gas from Russia after 30 days of the enactment of the Act.

China and India are the top two importers of Russian oil and India’s rising dependence on Russian oil shows it cannot quickly cut back on this source at a time when supplies through the Strait of Hormuz are still constrained.

The premium Russia has charged India for its oil has been steadily declining, the data shows, from $77.7 per tonne in April 2026 to $10.6 per tonne in June. Russia had been providing India a discount until as recently as February 2026.

India’s sanctions exposure

The Bill also specifies that tariffs could be imposed on countries that have helped Russia evade sanctions. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG) told The Hindu that India has specifically taken measures to pre-empt any sanctions exposure.

“It [sanctions exposure] was pre-empted through ship-to-ship transfer operations in international waters via the Red Sea route through Yanbu and Fujairah precisely so that a single choke point, or a single sanctions regime, could not halt India-bound cargo,” MoPNG said in a clarificatory note it had sent The Hindu in late July.

It is unclear as of now whether India’s actions would entail helping Russia evade sanctions.

Deepening concentration

Apart from Russia, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) too saw its share in India’s oil imports rise to historic highs. India sourced 17.5% of its oil imports by volume from the UAE in June 2026 and 18% by value, the highest share for both so far.

Taken together, this means that Russia and the UAE together accounted for nearly two-thirds of India’s oil imports in June 2026, the highest-ever combined share enjoyed by any two countries. The MoPNG, however, said that such concentration was not a matter of concern given Indian oil marketing companies stand ready to diversify quickly.

“Indian refineries had spent a decade acquiring the logistical flexibility to switch between crude grades and shipping routes the moment disruption struck, which is the definition of a diversification strategy, not its absence,” the note said.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 16 LIVE: The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026' passed in LS; RS passes The Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026'
World.content:
Both Houses saw couple of disruptions on Monday (August 10, 2026), Lok Sabha was adjourned minutes after the proceedings began at 11 a.m., amid protests from the Opposition demanding discussions on various issues. Rajya Sabha was also adjourned a few minutes later. Both Houses reconvened at 12 p.m. Lok Sabha introduced four Bills amid protests- The Tribunal Reforms Bill, 2026, the Minerals and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 and The National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026. Rajya Sabha briefly took up some business, but was adjourned minutes later.

Floor leaders of the Opposition parties held a meeting in the chamber of the Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, to chalk out the strategy for the Floor of the House on Monday (August 10, 2026).

The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 is also expected to be taken up in the discussion of the Opposition leaders. The Lok Sabha is scheduled to take up the introduction of several key bills on Monday, including the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, and the National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026.

World.title: Parliamentary panel flags critical gaps in Kerala’s disaster management framework
World.content:
Even as recurring extreme-weather events continue to bring Kerala to its knees, with back-to-back disasters striking the State during successive monsoon seasons, a report on disaster management tabled in the Rajya Sabha by the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs has identified gaps in Kerala’s disaster management framework.

Despite Kerala’s vulnerability to multiple hazards, including floods, landslides, coastal erosion, lightning and cyclonic events, the committee found that gaps persist in the last-mile dissemination of early warnings in landslide-prone and remote areas.

Technological limitations remain in areas such as hyper-local weather prediction, landslide early-warning accuracy and real-time flood-inundation modelling. High population density, environmental degradation and urban encroachment in ecologically sensitive areas continue to exacerbate disaster risks. Enforcement of building regulations, land-use planning norms and coastal regulation provisions also remains uneven, particularly at the local level, the committee observed, while it suggesting to strengthen the public awareness on multi-hazard warning systems.

Unique geography

According to the report, Kerala’s unique geographical setting, characterised by a narrow coastal belt, dense river network, ecologically fragile Western Ghats and high population density, results in overlapping hazard exposures, particularly during intense monsoon periods. Approximately 14.5% of the State is flood-prone, 14.4% is landslide-prone and more than half of its coastline is vulnerable to coastal hazards, it said.

However, the committee lauded Kerala’s decentralised disaster management framework, under which Disaster Management Plans are prepared at the State, district and Local Self-Government (LSG) levels. These plans are reviewed after every major disaster and updated annually through the ‘Orange Book’, an operational document integrating response strategies, financial provisions and departmental responsibilities.

Systems lauded

The committee also appreciated the State’s advanced early-warning and monitoring systems, particularly the ‘Kerala Warning, Crisis and Hazard Management’ (KaWaCHaM) system, which integrates multi-hazard alerts covering floods, landslides, storms and tsunamis. Technologies such as GIS-based hazard mapping, remote sensing, flood modelling and landslide early-warning systems were also lauded.

The strong role played by community volunteers, including Aapda Mitra volunteers and large-scale voluntarism networks, in augmenting the State’s response capacity was also praised. More than 4,500 trained volunteers are actively engaged in first response, particularly during floods and landslides.

The committee, however, noted that gaps persist despite Kerala developing a comprehensive and decentralised disaster management model integrating community participation, technology and anticipatory planning. It called for sustained efforts to strengthen risk-informed development norms, technological capabilities for forecasting and modelling, last-mile connectivity and public awareness, along with addressing the flaws in the land-use and construction practices being followed in the State.

Speaking to The Hindu, Kerala State Disaster Management Authority member secretary Sekhar L. Kuriakose said curbing inappropriate land use and construction practices and improving public awareness were among the issues the State government needed to address as per the report.

Improving forecast accuracy, including hyper-local weather prediction, was the responsibility of the Union government, as meteorological organisations fall under Entry 53 of List I (Union List), he said.

“The State will seriously take note of the suggestions and improve its part, while the forecast-related issues are expected to be addressed by the Centre,” Mr. Kuriakose said.

World.title: Woman farmer breaks down as over 100 trees felled for power tower in Kallakurichi
World.content:
A woman farmer broke into tears after more than a hundred trees that she had nurtured for years were cut down to make way for a high-tension electricity tower at Vadathorasalur in Kallakurichi district on Saturday (August 8, 2026).

The farmer, Selvi, along with her son Balamurugan, a dentist, had maintained a diverse and naturally cultivated farm of over 100 trees, including mango, teak, mahogany, and papaya. The trees had been growing on her farmland for over 10 years and were raised in memory of her late husband.

Officials from the Tamil Nadu Generation and Distribution Corporation (TANGEDCO) had recently inspected the land to set up a high-tension power tower and transmission line for the Thiyagadurgam area.

Selvi had requested the district authorities to shift the power line slightly so as not to disturb the trees. While officials had reportedly assured her that an alternative route would be arranged, they went ahead and felled the trees.

The trees were cut down using machinery right in front of Selvi and Balamurugan. While Selvi clung to the trees, police personnel forcibly removed her. A video of the incident has since gone viral.

Speaking to reporters, Selvi said the officials and police had acted in an inhumane manner. She said that while the government promotes tree-planting programmes on the one hand, it was destroying trees nurtured over 10 years.

The trees were worth an estimated ₹2 crore, but TANGEDCO officials stated that only ₹97,000 would be given as compensation, Balamurugan said. The compensation should be paid fairly, as had been done in other districts, and alternative routes should be planned so that trees on agricultural land are not affected, he said.

World.title: ‘Hail Mary’: First look of Kunchacko Boban’s next out
World.content:
The first look of the Kunchacko Boban starrer Hail Mary was released on Saturday (August 8) on Instagram. Directed by debutante Vishnu Revikumar, the film is jointly produced by Martin Prakkat Films and Green Room Productions.

The screenplay of Hail Mary, which is based on a novel by writer-director GR Indugopan, is written by Martin Prakkat and Dr Neeraj Rajan, who has co-written films such as Dominic and the Ladies’ Purse (2025) and ABCD (2013).

Other actors in the cast include Suraj Venjaramoodu, Anu Sithara, Suhasini Maniratnam, Hakkim Shajahan and Vinay Forrt, among others.

Roby Varghese Raj is the cinematographer of the film, which is edited by Chaman Chakko. Jakes Bejoy handles Hail Mary’s Music.

Hail Mary is the third collaboration between Kunchacko and Martin after Nayattu and Officer on Duty. Kunchacko was most recently seen in Unmadham, a psychological thriller, directed by Kiran Das and written by Shahi Kabir.

The Hindu review of Unmadham said, “With ‘meta’ written all over the film, Unmadham is not just about the struggles of a police officer who aspires to be in the film industry. It can also be seen as a commentary on the glut of police procedurals based on real-life cases, with the only idea left to be turned into a film being a case file that has superstitious fears attached to it. Unmadham goes into the deep recesses of a creative police officer’s mind, but manages to come up with only a few interesting crumbs.”

World.title: Iran says Pak-Saudi-Turkiye deal shows 'change in perception' towards US
World.content:
Iran’s foreign ministry said on Monday that the defence pact signed last week between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye was “a sign of a change in the perception” of regional countries towards the United States.

The joint defence agreement, signed in Makkah on Friday, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

“This development is a sign of a change in the perception of the countries of the region,” ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said while responding to a query during a weekly press briefing on Monday.

“Considering the developments of the last two to three years, the countries of the region have realised that security is not a commodity that can be bought from false security brokers,” Iran’s state media quoted him as saying, referring to the United States.

Baqaei further said that there was “no reason to worry that this treaty will be against Iran”, highlighting Iran’s deep religious, historical and civilisational ties with Pakistan, Turkiye and even Saudi Arabia.

“This development is an important sign that the countries of the region have concluded that they cannot rely on and trust the claim of security provided by the United States and some other actors outside the region, and they are attempting to try another method; by relying on their own capabilities and perspectives,” IRNA quoted Baqaei as saying.

“Any plan that is based on the geopolitical and historical realities of the region, is comprehensive and inclusive, and correctly identifies the enemy and the threat, has a chance of helping to strengthen security and prevent instability and abuses by the Zionist enemy and its allies,” he added, referring to Israel.

In response to a question about Iran’s willingness to possibly join the joint pact, Baqaei said Iran has always “emphasised pursuing security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries” and “free from the influence and destructive intervention” of foreign actors.

“Those plans still exist and can certainly be updated in light of developments,” the spokesperson added.

“We are in close contact with neighbouring countries and regional countries, and we hope that all countries will learn from the developments of the last two or three years and adopt the best path to strengthen the region’s collective security,” he said, according to IRNA.

Asked about Pakistan’s invitations to Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to visit Pakistan, Baqaei said, “This visit will take place whenever the time is right. Bilateral relations are mainly considered.”

He added: “The relationship between Iran and Pakistan is a very important one. In the last seven or eight months, it has become even more important than before, for various reasons.”

On Sunday, Deputy Prime Minister and FM Ishaq Dar said that the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement remained “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles after the Turkish foreign minister said Egypt could be joining the pact.

Dar said the pact was the “culmination of years of discussions and coordination”, adding that it was “purely defensive” in nature.

“It is not targeted against any country and its sole purpose is to further strengthen our ongoing efforts towards peace, stability and prosperity in the wider region.”

The deputy PM clarified that the pact did not abrogate or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between the signatory countries, or with other countries or organisations.

Dar speaks with Kuwait FM, others on pact

Separately, DPM Dar received a phone call from Kuwait’s Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, wherein the latter felicitated the former on the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Monday.

According to the FO, the two dignitaries spoke late on Sunday and also “exchanged views on the regional situation, including occupied East Jerusalem”.

They also discussed bilateral relations between the two countries and “matters of mutual interest, including the follow-up to FM Jarrah’s recent visit to Pakistan and further enhancing cooperation and investment in key sectors”.

“The two sides agreed to remain closely engaged,” the FO added.

The deputy premier also shared the contours of the pact with Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi and former Guinea-Bissau president General Umaro Sissoco Embaló.

In a joint call with them late last night, Dar shared the agreement’s “significance for strengthening strategic cooperation and contributing to regional peace, stability and security”, FO said.

Dar and Tshisekedi also exchanged views on Pakistan-DRC relations and agreed on the importance of further strengthening bilateral cooperation, including through high-level exchanges.

DPM Dar had also spoken to Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand a day ago.

“The two exchanged views on the regional situation, including the recently signed Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye,” the FO said.

It added that Dar shared the “essence of the agreement” and the “joint resolve of the three countries to contribute to regional peace, stability and security”.

World.title: 3rd phase of AJK polls: PPP continues to allege rigging as voting under way in Poonch Division's Bagh, Haveli
World.content:
The third phase of elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) is currently underway in four constituencies in Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts, with the PPP alleging rigging in the fresh round of polls as well.

Polling began at 8am and will continue until 5pm.

Government officials have anticipated clashes in some areas, while the Election Commission has classified most of the 803 polling stations in the four constituencies as either sensitive or highly sensitive.

“Apart from the regular police of both districts, we have dispatched an additional 10,300 troops to maintain law and order and provide a fear-free atmosphere to voters,” Election Commission Secretary Raja Mohammad Shakeel told Dawn earlier.

Elections are being held across AJK in phases amid tensions between protesters and the authorities. Polling in Mirpur and Muzaff­arabad divisions was held on July 27 and Aug 2, respectively, with the PML-N securing 24 seats. The PPP has only secured 10 seats so far.

The third phase of the polls was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division. The division comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district.

However, last week the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli due to concerns over the law and order situation. The AJK election commissioner has hinted that polling on the remaining seven constituencies could be held by Aug 20 or 21.

Malpractice, rigging allegations

Polling in previous phases of the elections was marred by allegations of rigging, scuffles and violence, with the PPP and the PML-N — the main contenders in AJK but allies in the Centre — engaging in a war of words.

The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging and electoral malpractices in the previous phases. It continued to allege rigging in Haveli and Bagh as well.

In a series of posts on X, the PPP shared complaints it said it had filed to the Election Commission.

In one of the complaints, the PPP alleged that roads leading to the Banni Marasira area had been blocked, where PML-N supporters were illegally stamping ballot papers at 12 polling stations in the LA-15 constituency.

“The commission is requested to consider the two acts together rather than separately, because the second is made possible by the first,” the party said, adding that officials, voters, polling agents and party workers were unable to reach the polling stations “to see what is being done inside”.

The party also claimed delays in polling at LA-15’s polling station no.87 in Thub. It also alleged that polling at stations no.143 and 144 in Hatala Pader did not commence on time due to the non-arrival of polling staff.

The PPP also alleged that its polling agent was “forcibly removed” from LA-15’s station no.158 in Makhdoom Kot. Similarly, PPP’s agents had also been removed from polling stations no.8-14 in Bani Maldhara and PML-N supporters were stamping ballot papers at those stations, the party alleged.

At around 12:45, the party claimed on X that workers of Jamaat-i-Islami had gathered to “capture” 26 polling stations in the constituency — nos.31-38, nos.70-79 and nos.180-186. It said the police had initially arrived but then withdrew.

“The stations are, therefore, unguarded at this moment, with an organised body assembled against them.”

It urged the Election Commission to determine on whose orders police had withdrawn and direct the law enforcers to return to the station.

The PPP also posted a blurry video, which it said was of PML-N workers “attacking” the polling station set up at the Boys Middle School in LA-15 Central Bagh.

Regarding LA-16, the party claimed that its polling agents were not being allowed inside stations no.119 and 120 while PML-N supporters were stamping ballot papers inside the stations in the agents’ absence.

The PPP further alleged delays in polling at stations no.61 and 141 of the constituency.

It made similar allegations regarding polling stations no.109 and 110 in LA-16 Bagh-III Sharqi. Moreover, the party accused “armed individuals associated with the PML-N” of opening fire at polling station no.179, Kot Chinalla in the constituency and disrupting the election process.

“The polling agents of the PPP have been removed from the station. It is further alleged that ballot papers are being stamped lawfully,” the PPP added.

In LA-17, the party alleged that its agents had been “forced out” from the polling station in Mullah Basti, Kahuta City by PML-N workers.

PPP Vice President Sherry Rehman expressed reservations after reports of rigging and malpractices emerged, saying that preventing polling agents from entering polling stations in LA-16 raised “serious questions” about the transparency of the election process.

In a statement, she demanded that an explanation be sought from the presiding officers of stations nos.119 and 120 on the matter.

The senator also called for the Election Commission to take notice of the reports of PPP’s polling agent being removed from station no.158 in LA-15.

Rehman further demanded alternative arrangements to compensate for the shortage of polling staff and material, calling on the authorities to ensure that free and transparent elections were held at all polling stations without any disruption.

PPP Secretary General Nayyar Bokhari also accused the PML-N of continuing rigging in the third phase of the elections. He highlighted that his party was regularly informing the Election Commission about the alleged rigging via phone.

But, “the chief election commissioner and the election commission secretary’s reply to all of our complaints has been that nothing has happened and everything is good,” he claimed.

When Dawn approached the Election Commission regarding Bokhari’s claim, Secretary Raja Muhammad Shakeel said any complaint that he or the chief election commissioner received was being attended and responded to, and the Quick Response Force (QRF) was also moved over it.

Rathore, two ex-AJK PMs face crucial electoral test

In Monday’s polls, AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, who is from the PPP, and two of his predecessors — Sardar Tanveer Ilyas and Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan — face a battle for political survival as voters head to the polls.

Around 238,664 men and 221,707 women are eligible to cast their ballots at 803 polling stations comprising 1,254 polling booths.

A total of 82 candidates are in the fray, with LA-14 (Dhirkot) attracting the highest number of candidates at 30 and LA-17 (Haveli) the lowest at nine.

In LA-17, Rathore is facing PML-N candidate Mohsin Aziz and independent candidate Khawaja Tariq Saeed, a member of the AJK Council.

Rathore and Saeed had been political allies and, under an agreement, had agreed to contest the seat alternately. However, after becoming prime minister, Rathore asked Saeed to step aside in his favour, a request he did not accept, turning the former allies into rivals.

Aziz, whose father Chaudhry Mohammad Aziz had won the seat at least three times, draws support from the sizeable Gujjar community. His recent large election rally in Forward Kahuta reportedly surprised his rivals and underscored the strength of his campaign.

Saeed, meanwhile, is believed to enjoy the backing of a sizeable section of the Kashmiri community, as well as an alliance of several smaller clans.

Rathore, however, remains confident of retaining the seat, citing the performance of his government during his relatively brief tenure as prime minister.

The constituency has also witnessed allegations of electoral irregularities on social media, with reports claiming that two presiding officers had been caught manipulating results in favour of Rathore. Shakeel dismissed the allegations but at the same time confirmed that complaints had been received against the two officials and that they had subsequently been relieved of election duties.

In LA-15 (Wasti Bagh), ex-PM Ilyas is facing PML-N candidate and former minister Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas, PPP nominee and sitting minister Sardar Ziaul Qamar, and Jamaat-i-Islami candidate retired Brig Dr Mohammad Khan, a respected educationist.

Ilyas, who secured a little over 3,300 votes from Upper Neelum in the second phase of the elections, had initially announced a boycott of the third phase. He subsequently reversed the decision and resumed campaigning, claiming that his victory would enable the constituency to “secure either the presidency or prime ministership.”

Ilyas and Qamar belong to the same Madiyal tribe, while Brig Khan belongs to the Narma clan and enjoys the support of former JI chief Abdul Rashid Turabi and former adviser Raja Yasin Khan.

Minhas has the advantage of belonging to the PML-N, which is poised to form the next government after emerging as the largest party in the elections held so far. His campaign has also stressed the argument that voters should elect a candidate from the party that is set to occupy the government benches rather than send their representative to the opposition.

In LA-16 (Sharqi Bagh), former ministers Sardar Mir Akbar and Sardar Qamar Zaman are the principal contenders, representing the PML-N and PPP, respectively.

The fourth contest, LA-14 (Dhirkot), has drawn particular attention because of the challenge faced by Sardar Attique, head of the once-dominant Muslim Conference (MC).

Attique is reportedly facing a strong challenge from Sajid Iqbal Abbasi of the relatively new Awam Dast-o-Bazu Party. A contractor and philanthropist, Abbasi is said to have spent millions of rupees from his own resources on public welfare projects in the constituency, helping him build a sizeable personal following.

Attique, who has represented the constituency successively since 2006, when he first became prime minister, faces an additional challenge in that Abbasi also belongs to the same tribe.

Among nearly two dozen other candidates are PML-N’s nominee Raja Faisal Azad and PPP candidate Raja Mubashar Ejaz. While the main contest is seen as being between Attique and Abbasi, the PML-N and PPP nominees are expected to vie for the second runner-up position.

Additional reporting by Tariq Naqash

World.title: Security forces kill 5 terrorists in intelligence-based operation in Balochistan's Panjgur
World.content:
Security forces have killed five terrorists, including a key commander, in an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in the Sarkini and Chedgi areas of Panjgur district in Balochistan, Radio Pakistan reported on Monday.

The operation was conducted as part of Operation Radd-ul-Fitna-3 in Balochistan, the state broadcaster said.

“According to security sources, the security forces conducted an intelligence-based operation against Fitna al Hindustan terrorists in Sarkani and Chedgi areas of Panjgur, killing five terrorists, including a key Fitna al Hindustan commander, Wazir,” it said.

Fitna al-Hindustan is a term used by the Pakistani military for India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation in Pakistan.

“Four motorcycles, machine guns, heavy weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the slain terrorists,” Radio Pakistan reported.

The terrorists were allegedly involved in robbery, extortion, kidnapping and attacks targeting local traders and other residents in Panjgur, it added.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi lauded security forces on the successful operation, according to state-run APP. Paying tribute to the professionalism and operational capabilities of the security forces, Naqvi said the successful action had thwarted the nefarious designs of the terrorists and dealt a major blow to their activities in the region.

Naqvi said the successful operation demonstrated the security forces’ preparedness, professionalism and unwavering commitment to combating terrorism. He stressed that the elimination of terrorist elements was essential for restoring lasting peace and stability in Balochistan and across the country.

He said the government and the people remained committed to supporting the security forces in their efforts to eradicate terrorist networks and ensure peace and security throughout the country.

The operation comes a day after security forces killed 15 terrorists in multiple intelligence-based operations across Balochistan. The operations were conducted in Mastung, Bolan, Washuk, Awaran, Sibi, Khuzdar, Harnai and Nushki under Operation Radd-ul-Fitna-3, according to state media.

The latest operations by the security forces in Balochistan take place as the province continues to face security challenges.

According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’ (PICSS) monthly security assessment released on July 31, the security situation deteriorated most significantly in Balochistan in the country last month.

The overall death toll increased by 241pc in Balochistan, from 109 in June to 372 in July, the report said.

Security personnel deaths in Balochistan increased from six in June to 62 in July, representing a rise of 933pc. Terrorist deaths rose from 75 to 238, while civilian deaths increased by 93pc, from 28 to 54. Eighteen members of peace committees were also killed in the province.

World.title: Delay in judicial appointments: IHC tells govt to explain consequences of keeping PM's advice pending
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Monday issued a ruling on a public interest petition challenging President Asif Ali Zardari’s delay in approving judicial appointments, directing the government to explain the constitutional consequences of keeping the premier’s advice pending for an indefinite period.

Justice Arbab Muhammad Tahir, who had reserved the order on the maintainability of the petition on August 6, issued notices to the president, the federation of Pakistan and the attorney general. He directed them to file separate concise reports explaining the timeline and status of the summary forwarded by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for judicial appointments.

The petition was filed by advocate Luqman Zafar through his counsel Zahid Asif Chaudhry amid a presidential delay in approving the judicial appointments recommended by the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP).

The JCP, headed by Chief Justice Yahya Afridi, recommended the appointment of 19 additional judges and the confirmation of five judges to high courts during meetings on July 20 and 21. The summary was subsequently forwarded by PM Shehbaz to President Zardari for assent under Article 48 of the Constitution. However, the president has yet to assent to the summary.

Last week, the IHC had reserved its verdict on the maintainability of the plea.

During Monday’s hearing, the petitioner’s counsel contended that Article 48(1) of the Constitution employed the expression “shall,” which cast a constitutional obligation upon the president to act on the advice of the prime minister.

The proviso to Article 48(1) allows the advice to be returned for reconsideration “within 15 days,” after which the president must act within ten days on the advice tendered after reconsideration.

The counsel relied on precedent to argue that the president was bound to act on the advice of the prime minister and could not convert the constitutional process into a power of indefinite deferral or veto.

It was further argued that the prolonged delay in implementing judicial appointments adversely impacted the administration of justice and affected the fundamental right of the public to timely access to justice, particularly when the superior courts are already burdened with an increasing backlog of cases.

Justice Tahir directed that notices be served through all modes of service, and Additional Attorney General Rashid Hafeez was directed to ensure that the respondents filed separate concise reports explaining the dates on which the advice was submitted to the president and the action, if any, taken thereon. The case was listed for hearing for August 11 (tomorrow).

The delay has already created practical complications. Four additional judges of the Peshawar High Court (PHC), whose confirmations were recommended by the JCP, ceased to hold office after their tenure expired on August 4 due to the absence of formal notifications.

Similarly, an additional judge of the Sindh High Court (SHC), whose term was extended by six months, relinquished office after his tenure expired on July 29.

The oath-taking ceremony for the newly recommended judges was scheduled for July 27 but was indefinitely postponed after President Zardari neither granted assent to the summary nor returned it, allegedly holding it “without any legal justification.

World.title: Indian students step up exam protests in Jharkhand, march towards state assembly
World.content:
Indian students marched towards the state assembly in Jharkhand on Monday, escalating protests over alleged irregularities in government recruitment examinations, with several students also on hunger strike.

Protests in Ranchi, capital of the eastern state home to more than 33 million people, began on July 29, days after a youth-led “cockroach” movement in New Delhi forced the resignation of the national education minister.

At least six protesters are on hunger strike, including student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, 33, who has been fasting for more than a week.

“We want the whole system to change,” Mahto said, as quoted by Indian media, demanding an end to the use of a private company that conducts tests for state civil service.

On Monday, hundreds of police guarded the assembly behind barbed-wire barricades, after repeated talks between the protesters and the state government failed to reach an agreement.

Large crowds of students chanting slogans marched towards the state assembly.

The protesters are demanding the cancellation of several examinations conducted by a private company on behalf of the state government, as well as an investigation by federal police into their conduct.

Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren has sought to defuse the protests by accepting some demands, while several members of the civil service body overseeing the examinations have stepped down.

“Every problem can be resolved through dialogue,” Soren said in a speech on Sunday.

The New Delhi protesters, organised by the online Cockroach Janta Party, rallied for 36 days over alleged failures in India’s examination system, before the then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan stepped down —giving the movement an unusual victory and turning examination integrity into a major political issue.

The Jharkhand protests echo those demands, reflecting wider frustration among young Indians who see government examinations as a key route to employment in a country where millions compete for limited public-sector jobs.

The New Delhi protests challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), but the Jharkhand rallies are demanding change from the state government, which stands in opposition to the BJP.

World.title: Rs115bn WB-funded rehabilitation project restructured quietly
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Amid a blame game and fiduciary concerns, the government has quietly restructured the Rs115 billion World Bank-funded post-flood rehabilitation project, depriving more than 134,000 verified flood-affected families in Balochistan of the resilient homes they were promised.

Official documents and background discussions indicate that investigations were underway into alleged record tampering, duplicate claims and multiple payments for the same housing units. There were also recorded attempts to disrupt such probes.

The project steering committee (PSC), led by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti, has now capped the $155 million housing component of the $400m Integrated Flood Resilience & Adaptation Project (IFRAP) at about 69,000 homes. The World Bank has consequently dropped its proposed $180m additional financing that could have extended reconstruction to the remaining affected families.

After the devastating 2022 floods, Pakistan secured more than $9bn in international pledges at the January 2023 Geneva Conference. IFRAP was designed to rebuild homes in Balochistan through a community-led, owner-driven model. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had publicly promised a resilient house for every family that lost one. Yet at its June 22-23 meeting, the PSC unanimously redirected the remaining housing funds towards roads and irrigation and formally declined additional World Bank financing.

Over 134,000 flood-hit families in Balochistan being affected amid investigations of record tampering, duplicate claims

The decision reverses that commitment, despite more than 134,000 verified families having been surveyed and registered for assistance.

PSC meeting minutes showed the planning minister expressed concern over “misreporting” of completed houses as “the number of completed houses presented to the Prime Minister was 15,000 whereas official reports reflected 8,694 completed houses”.

There are conflicting arguments – one side claiming misreporting to downgrade housing project for ‘redirecting’ funds to contractor-oriented larger infrastructure project and the other side showing concern over slow pace of house completion in four years due to lack of land titles, access to financial accounts and transparency. The planning commission has now proposed satellite imagery for verification.

Both the minister and the CM ordered an independent high-level inquiry to ensure transparency and accountability. The committee also noted serious corruption charges against certain officials but the fact finding committee could not be given access to records in Balochistan.

Not only this, the ministries of planning and economic affairs appeared at different wavelength. The EAD put on record that the WB had expressed concerns over changes in project leadership arrangements. Clearly, the bank and the planning commission apparently had their own priorities for the project leadership.

Informed source said the minister for planning and WB country director Bolormaa Amgaabazar have had at least two meetings to clear the situation but issues continue to prolong.

Interestingly, a similar project, the Sindh People’s Housing for Flood Affectees (SPHF) involving around $3bn funding and over 2m home reconstructions, goes on and presents a success story though the planning commission remains unhappy without a third-party verification.

When contacted, the commission said the inclusive development programme “under IFRAP was damaged in a coordinated manner for vested interests by shifting financing from important sectors i.e. education, health, PHE, irrigation, bridges, roads, livelihood and youth skill development to housing to show burn rate”.

The commission denied that housing project had been stopped, adding that about 75,000 fully damaged houses were under construction, 26,000 of them completed. It said the project originally approved by Ecnec was 68,922 that would remain protected. It said vested interests planned diversion of funds from early warning system, irrigation etc to housing in violation of Ecnec approved scope. It reported that out of total $400m IFRAP envelope, $245m had already been signed.

It said the allegation of misreporting of 15,000 completed houses to PM was raised by a local parliamentarian, and inquiry established misrepresentation.

About different treatments to two similar projects in Sindh and Balochistan, the commission said they were incomparable, as IFRAP in Balochistan was a federal budget project with a single WB loan on federal government and involved budgetary disbursement and compliance requirements while Sindh was a direct borrower from multiple lenders and financed through section 42 entity – a non-profit non-binding disbursement schedules.

Published in Dawn, August 10th, 2026

World.title: Malaysia PM Anwar Ibrahim undergoes elective surgery to treat hernia
World.content:
Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has successfully undergone elective laparoscopic surgery to treat a para-umbilical hernia, his medical team said on Monday.

“He is currently undergoing physiotherapy treatment and is under the supervision of a team of medical experts to ensure that the recovery process is going well”, the head of Anwar’s medical team, Sri Ranga Abdullah Ramaiah, said in a statement.

Earlier on Monday, Anwar’s aide said the premier was undergoing medical checks and was expected to be under observation for two days.

“Let us pray … that he is blessed with long-lasting health so that he can return to his usual duties in the near future,” Press Secretary Tunku Nashrul Abaidah said.

Meanwhile, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif wished his Malaysian counterpart a speedy recovery.

In a post on X, he said: “Wishing my dear brother, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, a swift and smooth recovery during his medical procedures.”

“The people of Pakistan join me in praying for his continued good health and well-being,” he added.

Anwar, who turned 79 on Monday and has been in office since 2022, has had recurrent shoulder and back problems. He was hospitalised in 2018 for shoulder and back pain. Last November, he cancelled a trip to Pahang state due to back pain.

In January, he was issued a clean bill of health after undergoing a routine medical examination, according to a hospital statement.

World.title: High court judge to investigate Mir Raza murder case, says home minister
World.content:
• Announcement comes hours after Faryal Talpur recommends judicial probe

• Previous investigation body sent packing as IGP forms new team

• DSP, Jauhar SHO suspended for failing to preserve crime scene

• Sharjeel moves NCCIA over ‘defamatory campaign’

KARACHI: In what appears to be a damage-control exercise, the provincial government has decided to conduct a judicial inquiry by a judge of the Sindh High Court into the murder of young businessman Mir Raza Ali, a day after a fresh autopsy ruled out the possibility of suicide on the grounds that he had been shot in the back and that his body bore marks of torture.

An announcement to this effect was made by Sindh Home Minister Zia Lanjar a few hours after senior Pakistan Peoples Party leader and chairperson of the Sindh Assembly’s Standing Committee on Home Affairs, Faryal Talpur, recommended that the chief minister constitute a judicial commission to conduct a transparent, impartial and comprehensive investigation into the case.

An IBA graduate and owner of the eatery Wafflix, Mir Raza had gone missing on July 28, and his body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar.

When investigators reportedly focused their probe on the possibility of suicide and reports emerged about a flawed autopsy, Raza’s family filed an application before a judicial magistrate seeking the exhumation of the body for a fresh post-mortem examination.

While the magistrate ordered the exhumation, the provincial government changed the composition of the medical board three times, fuelling rumours that there was an attempt to cover up the case. Later, the government restored the original medical board that had carried out the exhumation and conducted the autopsy and found that he had suffered injuries and had been shot in the back.

On Sunday, in an attempt to show the public that there’s nothing to hide, senior PPP leader Faryal Talpur recommended a judicial commission, saying it should examine all aspects of the incident and bring the facts to light.

“Legal and disciplinary action should be taken without discrimination against those found responsible in light of the commission’s findings,” she added.

Talpur stressed that justice for the victim’s family must be ensured at all costs and that the public should be transparently informed of all facts surrounding the case.

“No negligence or bias will be tolerated in meeting the requirements of justice,” she said, adding that providing justice to the bereaved family and maintaining public confidence in the justice system were fundamental responsibilities of the government and relevant institutions.

A few hours after Talpur’s statement, Home Minister Lanjar and Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab reached deceased Raza’s residence, met with his father, Mir Hussain Ali, and assured the family that they would be provided complete justice.

Talking to the media after the meeting, Lanjar said a decision had been taken to conduct a judicial inquiry, under the supervision of a Sindh High Court judge, into the murder case.

He said a transparent and impartial investigation would be ensured.

Speaking on the occasion, Mayor Wahab noted that Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah chaired a four-hour-long meeting during which “all aspects of the incident and the investigation were reviewed in detail”.

New investigation team formed

The Sindh police chief dismissed the previous investigation team headed by Special Investigation Unit SSP Dr Samiullah Soomro and appointed DIG Amir Farooqi to lead a five-member new committee.

Other members of the committee are SSP Syed Muhammad Ali Raza, SP Qais Khan, SP Anam Tajjamul and Inspector Ch. Ghazanfar.

According to a notification, “The team shall undertake a comprehensive and impartial investigation into the case from all relevant angles. The team shall identify, collect, preserve and examine any new or additional evidence and shall thoroughly examine and analyse all physical, technical, circumstantial and forensic evidence collected during the investigation.

“The team shall make all-out efforts to work out the case and submit a report to the court concerned within the stipulated period. The team may co-opt any officer to assist in the investigation. Progress shall be reported on a day-to-day basis,” it added.

DSP, Jauhar SHO suspended

Karachi police chief Azad Khan has suspended Sharea Faisal DSP Muhammad Arshad Afridi and Gulistan-i-Jauhar SHO Kamran Qureshi with immediate effect.

A police spokesperson said that both officials were suspended for failing to preserve the crime scene and conduct a proper crime-scene investigation after the body of Mir Raza was found.

Sharjeel moves NCCIA against ‘malicious social media campaign’

Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon, through his counsel, filed an application before the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) against unknown persons for “causing harassment, creating false and malicious content on social media against him and his son.

The application stated that certain social media accounts began circulating posts, videos and statements against Memon and his son, containing “allegations that are false, baseless, fabricated, and malicious in nature, and which are calculated to injure their reputation, dignity, and standing in society”.

Memon stated that none of the allegations — that he owned the guest house in Gulistan-i-Jauhar, where Mir Raza was allegedly tortured and murdered and that his son had left for London immediately after the incident and has since been moving around with a bodyguard — has “any factual or evidentiary basis, and each is false, baseless, and malicious, being designed solely to malign” him and his son for extraneous political motives.

His lawyer asked the NCCIA to register an FIR and proceed in accordance with law against the persons found responsible under the applicable provisions of the Prevention of Electronic Crime Act 2016 and any other law found attracted.

Published in Dawn, August 10th, 2026

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.

Energy storage is another missing pillar. Solar and wind need storage support to become more reliable. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and other storage systems should be reduced to zero. This will help stabilise renewable power and support future grid flexibility.

Electric vehicles can also become part of the solution. In China, Japan, and the United States, EVs are increasingly seen as mobile energy storage systems. A typical EV battery has a capacity of 40–70 kWh, enough to power an average household for 1–2 days. If Bangladesh had 1 million EVs, the country would have 40–70 GWh of distributed storage. This is several times higher than the daily peak demand gap. Solar-powered EV charging, vehicle-to-home, and vehicle-to-grid systems should be included in future energy planning.

If Bangladesh had 30–40 percent of the grid powered by solar, along with solar-powered EVs, the country would be far less exposed to global fuel market shocks. Long fuel lines, online schooling, shorter office hours, and industrial disruption could be reduced. Solar, storage, and EVs should now be planned together.

Finance will decide how fast this transition happens. Renewable energy projects cannot grow at interest rates below 10–12 percent. Long-term financing should be available at an interest rate of 3.5–4.5 percent. A 10–15-year financing facility at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent should be introduced. Bangladesh Bank’s green refinancing fund should be expanded. Rooftop and residential solar customers should be eligible for collateral-free loans. The LC margin for renewable equipment should be limited to 5%.
